title: From Bits to Qubits: The Theory and Practice of Quantum Data Encoding
abstract: Encoding classical data into quantum systems is a foundational step in the execution of nearly all quantum algorithms, and a critical bottleneck in realizing practical quantum advantage. This review provides a comprehensive account of the concepts, algorithms, and practical considerations associated with quantum data encoding. We trace the development from its early conceptual foundations to recent advances, considering commonly used access models, such as quantum state preparation, unitary synthesis, QRAM and block encoding. We survey the circuit size, depth, space-time tradeoffs, as well as non-Clifford resources required for fault-tolerant implementation. We also discuss the roles of different access models in quantum algorithms. Special attention is given to structured data, such as sparse data, Boolean functions and data represented by tensor networks. This review bridges theory and applications, serving both as a pedagogical guide for newcomers and as a reference for active researchers. We also highlight the pivotal role of quantum data encoding in quantum computing and provide insights into future directions that will enable quantum advantage.

title: Bag of Tricks or Bag of Myths? Reducing Modeling Complexity with Task Knowledge in Explainable Suicide Risk Assessment
abstract: Assessing suicide risk from social media text is a small-data, high-stakes setting requiring not only severity prediction but also supporting evidence and clinically relevant risk and protective factors. Yet common NLP techniques, including model scaling, synthetic data, loss reweighting, ensembling, and threshold tuning, are often applied without testing whether their gains hold up under severe class imbalance, coupled outputs, and limited author-level data. We study 1,635 clinician-annotated posts and audit 31 pre-specified techniques from 7 methodological families through roughly 300 controlled experiments on author-disjoint partitions. We found no prior audit of this playbook in this regime. The findings guide a task-grounded system for three outputs: 4-level suicide risk, evidence spans, and 24 clinical risk and protective factors. Only 5 of 31 comparisons produced reliable gains. We reformulate factor prediction as entailment between each post and its codebook definitions, using an architecturally diverse ensemble with class-balanced training and score rescaling. title: Constrained Online Learning with Noisy Constraint Values
abstract: We study constrained online convex optimization with adversarial constraints and conditionally unbiased, finite-variance observations of constraint values and gradients. Under common feasibility, our \LEDGER\ algorithm attains $O(\sqrt T)$ expected regret and $O(\sqrt{T\log(eT)})$ expected budget violation, the largest cumulative overspend over any window. It uses a reflected exponential potential, clipped signed observations, and predictable adaptive regularization, with one feedback triple and one projection per round. Neither a Slater condition, independence between feedback channels, nor an absolute constraint-value bound is needed. A Gaussian testing lower bound proves that the budget rate has optimal horizon dependence under square-root regret at fixed positive noise, including the logarithm. The same obstruction holds for terminal violation, so the logarithm is not a cost of maximizing over windows; an $O(\sqrt T)$ budget bound instead forces linear regret. In contrast, fixed positive Gaussian value noise yields a joint regret--hard-violation lower bound of $Ω(\min\{σ,1\}T/\log^2 T)$, even with exact gradients in one dimension. The hard-violation construction matches arbitrarily many moments while preserving a feasible-endpoint gap and constant endpoint probabilities. Together, the bounds separate uncertainty about hard feasibility from learnable signed budgets. Deterministic restarts remove the horizon input without changing either upper rate.

title: Marginal Fidelity Does Not Establish User Simulation in Demographic Synthetic Survey Panels: Response Contracts, Support Collapse and Conditioning Failure
abstract: Demographic synthetic survey panels are often validated by matching aggregate answers to published surveys. We test what that certificate establishes across six multiselect batteries from four survey organisations in three countries. The headline analysis is restricted to three instruments whose synthetic cohort and human target share the stated population frame; three other batteries remain sensitivity analyses. The response contract dominates measured fidelity. In the aligned instruments, committed sets leave 66 of 128 model-battery option slots empty in panels of up to 500 respondents, versus 0 of 128 under per-option probability elicitation. Across eight uncapped model-instrument comparisons, probabilities reduce option-marginal MAE by 4.53 to 7.30 points. The capped instrument reverses on two models until the vectors are projected onto its stated maximum. These are measurement effects: human targets are realised check-all responses, whereas the vectors are latent inclusion propensities. Published marginal agreement also fails to discriminate respondent simulation from direct population estimation. On nine aligned model-battery pairs, a no-persona population-prevalence query averages 6.27 MAE versus 12.39 for committed panels and wins all nine comparisons. Constraint-aware probability vectors average 5.34 and beat the query on four of nine, so the baseline challenges the validation criterion rather than proving direct estimation uniformly best. On three unpublished demographic cells, neither approach beats reciting the national distribution. Population-marginal agreement is therefore evidence about an elicitation contract and an estimand obtainable without simulated respondents, not evidence of individual simulation.

title: Learning to Fly: Stable Vision-Guided UAV Servoing with Compact Target-Centric Cues and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Vision-guided reinforcement learning for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) remains challenging due to unstable policy optimisation, aggressive exploration, and the cost of high-dimensional visual perception. In this work, we investigate long-horizon UAV visual servoing using compact target-centric cues combined with low-dimensional sensor measurements. Rather than learning directly from RGB images, lightweight target segmentation provides image-space offsets and relative depth, which are combined with quadrotor velocity and projected-gravity measurements into a compact 12D policy observation. We compare Direct PPO with three matched-budget curriculum strategies: a Visual curriculum that progressively expands target placement difficulty, a Dynamics curriculum that gradually relaxes action constraints and smoothing, and a Joint curriculum that combines both progressions. All strategies reach comparable nominal performance, with complementary advantages across tracking metrics. Observation ablations show that proprioceptive measurements are critical for stable flight and image-space cues for target alignment, while explicit depth is not necessary for strong performance in the evaluated setting. Against tuned classical visual-servo controllers, learned policies show greater robustness to strong control and visual perturbations, while the Visual curriculum exhibits the smallest degradation under unseen target motion. Overall, the results demonstrate that compact target-centric representations can support robust long-horizon aerial visual servoing and that visual curriculum training can improve robustness to dynamic distribution shifts despite limited gains in nominal performance.

title: NeuCME: Toward Dynamic Multimodal Continual Learning via Neural Combinatorics of Multiple Experts
abstract: Multimodal continual learning has recently shown great potential for developing agents with human-like intelligence by continuously learning new tasks across multiple modalities. However, existing methods typically assume that the set of modalities per task is predefined and fixed. In this paper, we investigate a more realistic learning setting, referred to as dynamic multimodal continual learning, in which the set of modalities may vary across tasks rather than remaining fixed. This setting involves two primary challenges: (i) spatio-temporal catastrophic forgetting and (ii) adaptive multimodal fusion. To address these challenges, we propose NeuCME (as shorthand for \textbf{Neu}ral \textbf{C}ombinatorics of \textbf{M}ultiple \textbf{E}xperts), a novel framework designed to effectively learn and integrate knowledge across tasks with varying modalities. The proposed NeuCME model comprises three key components, namely modality-combinational rehearsal, multi-gated mixture-of-experts, and task relevance-guided distillation. Furthermore, we formulate an evaluation metric to quantify the dynamism of task sequences and then set up a comprehensive benchmark with different degrees of dynamism. Extensive experiments using four real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed NeuCME outperforms state-of-the-art methods markedly.

title: Robust Decentralized Federated Distillation via Multi-Modality Knowledge Collaboration
abstract: This paper propose a robust decentralized federated distillation method that enables clients with heterogeneous models to collaborate through predictions on shared unlabeled public data. In the proposed method, each client first evaluates the received predictions in three modalities of class prediction, boundary decision, and prediction correlation. It then filters unreliable clients, assigns reliability-based weights to the retained clients, and constructs a teacher for each type of knowledge. Finally, the corresponding distillation gradients are validated using a supervised gradient computed from private data. Conflicting prediction and boundary gradients are removed, and conflicting relation gradients are suppressed before the final model update. We prove the convergence of the proposed method by showing stable local optimization for honest clients under Byzantine distillation. Particularly, we show that our method ensures a bounded Byzantine influence on both distillation gradients and individual client private gradients after cross-modality fusion, thereby enabling stable local optimization for honest clienunder Byzantine distillation. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 demonstrate that the proposed method improves the prediction accuracy of heterogeneous models of clients under non-IID data and Byzantine attacks. As the booming demands of federated learning in decentralized environments such as edge computing and mission-oriented UAV collaborations, our method has a great potential for adoption of DFL in unreliable real-world scenarios where clients are exposed to receiver-specific Byzantine messages of malicious predictions.

title: OpenLogic : édition française — Des ensembles au calcul des séquents
abstract: Cette cinquième livraison française du manuel ouvert OpenLogic réunit six chapitres : ensembles, relations, fonctions, dénombrabilité, construction des nombres et ensembles infinis. Elle comprend 45 sections, 73 exercices et 51 des 722 unités prévues pour l'édition intégrale. Lecteur PDF, 79 pages LaTeX cumulatif complet Sources complètes et reconstruction PDF/EPUB EPUB 3 Les nouveaux chapitres construisent les entiers, les rationnels et les réels par les coupures de Dedekind et les suites de Cauchy, puis présentent l'hôtel de Hilbert, les algèbres de Dedekind, la récurrence et une autre démonstration de Schröder–Bernstein. Les corrections de la source et les précisions éditoriales sont signalées dans le texte. Le LaTeX cumulatif contient le texte complet et reproduit exactement le PDF publié. Le ZIP comprend les sources modulaires, les styles, les figures, les bibliographies, les scripts de reconstruction et les dépendances de conversion du projet. L'EPUB 3 contient 3 245 expressions MathML natives, 13 figures décrites, 73 exercices et 76 notes. Il passe EPUBCheck 5.3.0 sans erreur ni avertissement ; la lecture a été vérifiée sur écran large et étroit. Les fichiers des livraisons antérieures restent publics. Traduction et révision éditoriale assistées par IA, avec références françaises et décisions documentées. Aucune validation humaine indépendante n'est revendiquée. L'édition intégrale reste en cours. Miroir GitHub · Catalogue des traductions d'OpenLogic. Cette révision des fichiers rend également disponibles les LaTeX cumulatifs complets des trois premières livraisons : Ensembles (7 unités), Ensembles et Relations (16 unités), puis Ensembles, Relations et Fonctions (23 unités). Chacun reproduit exactement son PDF historique. Les ZIP correspondants conservent les styles, figures, bibliographies et instructions nécessaires. Les noms numérotés associent PDF, LaTeX et sources; tous les anciens liens restent accessibles. title: Operational Accessibility, State Economy, and the \delta^* Threshold Operator
abstract: Operational Accessibility, State Economy, and the \delta^* Threshold Operator Let an artificial cognitive or physical system at step t be described under a chosen representation space \mathcal{M} such that s_t = \pi(h_t) \in \mathcal{M}, where h_t \in \mathcal{H} represents the full historical trajectory of operations and observations. Rather than defining capability as an intrinsic vector of static functions assigned to an individuated agent, continuation is defined over an action space \mathcal{A} governed by an Admissibility Field \mathcal{F}_t = \{ a \in \mathcal{A} \mid \mathcal{C}(a \mid s_t, \mathcal{R}) \le \theta_{\text{adm}} \}, where \mathcal{R} denotes the local resource regime, \mathcal{C}: \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{M} \times \mathcal{R} \to \mathbb{R}^+ maps an operation to its execution cost, and \theta_{\text{adm}} is the strict admissibility boundary. A realised operation a_t \in \mathcal{F}_t produces a state update not by appending an informational token into a static memory buffer, but by transforming the geometry of \mathcal{F}_{t+1}; the fundamental unit of analysis is strictly the induced transition \mathcal{F}_t \xrightarrow{a_t} \mathcal{F}_{t+1}. Latent operational differences do not require postulating hidden ontologies: two histories h^{(1)} and h^{(2)} are operationally dormant under \pi if \pi(h^{(1)}) = \pi(h^{(2)}) = s and \mathcal{F}(s; \theta) \equiv \mathcal{F}^{(1)} = \mathcal{F}^{(2)}. The retuning operator \delta^* : \theta_{\text{adm}} \mapsto \theta_{\text{adm}} + \Delta \theta^* acts directly on the admissibility threshold such that \mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}(s) = \{ a \in \mathcal{A} \mid \mathcal{C}_{\delta^*}(a \mid s, \mathcal{R}) \le \theta_{\text{adm}} + \Delta \theta^* \}, causing previously indistinguishable trajectories to diverge interventionally (\mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}(h^{(1)}) \neq \mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}(h^{(2)})) without requiring retrospective modifications to the classical historical store. Conversely, the adjoint unlearning operator \delta^{*\dagger} renders an active operational distinction unreachable across all subsequent admissible continuations via \lim_{\delta^{*\dagger}} \mathcal{F}(s \oplus \Delta) \to \mathcal{F}(s). To determine whether an accessibility architecture provides genuine structural compression over unconstrained state expansion \mathcal{M}' \supset \mathcal{M}, the representation cost is quantified as the tuple \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}}(\mathcal{S}) = \langle d_{\text{eff}}(\mathcal{S}), B(\mathcal{S}), N_{\text{sample}}(\epsilon) \rangle, spanning effective tangent dimension d_{\text{eff}} = \operatorname{dim}(\operatorname{span}\{ \nabla_a \mathcal{C}(a \mid s) \mid a \in \mathcal{F}_{\delta^*} \}), boundary bit-depth B(\mathcal{S}) = \mathbb{I}(H_{\le t} ; \mathcal{F}_{> t}), and sample identification complexity N_{\text{sample}}, establishing strict superiority if and only if \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}}(\mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}) < \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}}(\mathcal{M}') at matched predictive divergence D_{\text{KL}} \le \epsilon. This architecture is empirically bounded by three protocols: Protocol I (Interventional Residue) falsifies persistence if a transported residue fails the mapping \mathcal{T}_{A \to B}(\mathcal{F}_A) = \mathcal{F}_B across distinct carriers; Protocol II (Regime Transformation) verifies that shifts in \delta^* alter the topology of reachable continuations rather than single-step token likelihoods; and Protocol III (Monitoring Depth Falsification) enforces a mandatory kill-switch, rejecting the accessibility hypothesis in favor of a minimal Markovian baseline whenever extending historical depth K > K_0 fails to produce a statistically significant reduction in \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}} or predictive error on held-out tasks.

title: Based on Particle-Group Complexity Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on particle-group dynamics, designed to automatically adjust particle group parameters and optimize complex models' performance. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter setting, while this algorithm dynamically adapts to the problem's characteristics. The core mechanism involves the algorithm's ability to self-adjust particle group parameters based on an internal simulation, allowing for efficient and robust optimization of complex models. The paper details the algorithm's design, its performance evaluation, and potential applications across diverse modeling domains.

title: 基于自适应的拓扑结构进化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm, termed "Adaptive Topology Evolution," designed to automatically explore and optimize topological structures. Traditional topological evolution methods often rely on manual design, limiting their applicability to complex systems. Our algorithm employs an adaptive approach, dynamically adjusting topology parameters through a self-learning process. This allows for the generation of robust and flexible topological models suitable for simulation and analysis. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of examples, showcasing its ability to discover and refine complex topological configurations. The core mechanism centers around a hierarchical structure that iteratively refines topology, fostering novel and optimized representations.

title: Based on Topological Logic: Distributed Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed artificial intelligence (DAI) leveraging the inherent parallelism of topological logic. Traditional DAI systems often struggle with computational bottlenecks and scalability limitations. This work addresses these challenges by formulating AI tasks as topological logic operations and executing them concurrently across a distributed network of nodes. The core mechanism involves decomposing complex AI problems into smaller, interconnected topological operations, facilitating efficient parallel computation and streamlined information exchange via topological communication protocols. We demonstrate the potential of this methodology to significantly enhance both the computational efficiency and scalability of DAI systems, ultimately paving the way for more robust and adaptable AI solutions. The system utilizes a graph-based representation for data and computations, enabling a natural mapping of AI algorithms onto topological logic operations. We explore the theoretical foundations of this approach and outline a framework for implementing and deploying topological logic-based DAI systems.

title: Quantum Noise Degradation and Error-Correcting Code Optimization in Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, but its inherent susceptibility to noise poses a significant challenge to achieving reliable computations. This work investigates the degradation of quantum information due to noise and proposes an optimized approach to error-correcting codes specifically tailored for quantum systems. We establish a precise noise degradation model, incorporating various noise types and their statistical properties, represented as (σi). This model allows for a more realistic simulation of quantum noise compared to traditional approaches. Subsequently, we employ an optimization algorithm, based on the principle of minimizing bit-flip error rates, to design error-correcting codes. The core of our design strategy leverages information theory concepts, particularly channel capacity and mutual information, represented as (Cch, Imn), to determine the optimal code parameters. The optimization process aims to find the most efficient code that can effectively protect quantum information from noise, ultimately enhancing the reliability of quantum computations. The final optimized code is characterized by its encoding rate (R), decoding rate (D), and the minimum distance (dmin) of the code, represented as (R, D, dmin). The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in mitigating noise degradation and improving the performance of quantum error correction.

title: Bio-Inspired Multi-Agent Evolutionary System (BMEIE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex problem-solving by leveraging the principles of biological multi-agent systems. The Bio-Inspired Multi-Agent Evolutionary System (BMEIE) constructs intricate systems capable of self-organization and adaptive learning through the emulation of evolutionary processes observed in natural systems such as ant colonies and fish schools. The core of BMEIE involves the integration of genetic algorithms, simulated annealing, and other optimization techniques to facilitate the evolutionary refinement of parameters and strategies within a multi-agent framework. This allows the system to collaboratively tackle intricate challenges. The system's adaptive and robust design stems from its unique combination of biological inspiration and advanced optimization methods. The research aims to establish a new paradigm for designing intelligent systems capable of autonomous learning and robust performance across diverse, dynamic environments. The system's effectiveness is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual demonstrations, highlighting its potential for a wide range of applications.

title: Bayesian Inference-Based Multi-Agent Collaborative Learning
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian inference techniques to facilitate multi-agent collaborative learning. Traditional multi-agent systems often struggle with efficient learning in dynamic and uncertain environments, particularly when agents need to coordinate their actions based on incomplete or noisy information. This research proposes a novel framework that leverages Bayesian networks (BNs) or Markov networks (MNs) to model and reason about the interactions between multiple agents. By explicitly representing dependencies and uncertainties through probabilistic graphical models, agents can effectively learn optimal collaborative strategies. The core claim is that this approach significantly enhances collaboration efficiency and overall performance compared to traditional methods. The key mechanism involves employing Bayesian inference to update agent beliefs about the states of other agents and the environment, leading to improved decision-making and coordination. This work highlights the potential of combining probabilistic reasoning with multi-agent systems for tackling complex collaborative problems.

title: Algorithmic Exploration of Complex Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper presents an algorithmic framework designed to enhance the exploration of complex evolutionary algorithms, specifically addressing the inherent challenges of navigating high-dimensional search spaces and identifying optimal solutions. The core mechanism centers around a novel 'genetic-inspired exploration' strategy that intelligently combines mutation and selection to facilitate a more efficient search. We propose a method for automatically identifying promising regions of the search space, reducing the need for extensive manual tuning and improving the overall performance of evolutionary algorithms. The goal is to provide a more robust and automated approach to optimization, offering a potential improvement over traditional methods. This work explores the design of a systematic process for guiding the evolutionary process, leading to better solutions in complex scenarios.

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Algorithm Implementation
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field of physics, offers a unique and potentially transformative approach to computation. This paper explores the concept of adaptive algorithms leveraging quantum topology to achieve enhanced computational precision and efficiency. We present a novel algorithm, designed to exploit the inherent dynamic nature of quantum states, forming a basis for adaptive computation. The core mechanism centers around constructing a quantum topology algorithm that responds to changes in the input, thereby optimizing the computation process. We argue that this approach represents a significant step forward from traditional algorithms, particularly in scenarios involving complex systems exhibiting dynamic properties.

title: Improved Secret Sharing Protocol Based on Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper presents an improved secret sharing protocol leveraging the principles of quantum decoherence. The core claim is to design a protocol that significantly reduces the number of shares required while maintaining the security of the secret. This is achieved through a novel approach to key partitioning and reconstruction based on the unique properties of quantum decoherence. The protocol minimizes redundancy within the shared key, thereby enhancing security. The key innovation lies in the application of quantum decoherence to fundamentally reduce the number of shares needed for a given secret, addressing limitations inherent in classical secret sharing schemes. The design incorporates error correction techniques alongside the decoherence-based key management, providing a robust solution. Mathematical formulations are provided to demonstrate the protocol's operation and security analysis. The theoretical analysis suggests a reduction in key size compared to traditional schemes, offering a potentially transformative approach to secure key distribution.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Simulating Quantum Circuit Evolution
abstract: Simulating the evolution of quantum circuits is a computationally intensive task, fundamentally limited by the need to explore the exponentially large Hilbert space associated with quantum systems. This work introduces a novel approach utilizing probabilistic programming to efficiently model and simulate quantum circuit dynamics. The core idea involves representing quantum circuit operations as probabilistic functions, enabling the use of Monte Carlo methods for estimating circuit evolution with significantly reduced computational overhead. This approach provides a flexible and scalable framework for exploring complex quantum systems, particularly those where traditional deterministic simulation methods become intractable. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline of implementation, highlighting potential benefits and future research directions. Key mathematical concepts employed include probability theory, Markov chains, and Monte Carlo integration. The primary goal is to offer a practical alternative to standard quantum simulation techniques, particularly for scenarios requiring approximate solutions or exploration of large parameter spaces.

title: Quantum Computation Based on Spin Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the development of a quantum computation model based on spin systems. The core principle leverages the quantum mechanical properties of spins – specifically, their ability to exist in superposition and entanglement – to perform computations. We propose a novel architecture utilizing coupled spins as qubits, exploring methods for controlled manipulation and measurement. The model is presented with a detailed mathematical formulation, including qubit representation, gate operations, and measurement probabilities. We analyze the potential advantages and challenges associated with this approach, emphasizing the need for robust control and error correction techniques. The research contributes to the broader exploration of alternative quantum computing paradigms beyond traditional superconducting and trapped ion technologies. The key mathematical elements are presented here, including qubit states, gate operations, and probability calculations, forming the basis of the proposed quantum computation model. ---

title: Circular Adaptive Quantum Geometry (ISAG)
abstract: This paper introduces Circular Adaptive Quantum Geometry (ISAG), a novel quantum geometric algorithm designed to automate the adjustment of geometric shapes, enabling high-precision and efficient geometric modeling and transformations. The core of ISAG lies in the implementation of a cyclical transformation process, guided by adaptive algorithms, which dynamically adjusts geometric parameters, resulting in more flexible and optimized transformation processes. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional geometric modeling techniques by offering a dynamic and self-correcting mechanism. The paper details the algorithm's design, its mathematical framework, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for significant improvements in geometric modeling efficiency. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, highlighting its strengths and potential applications across various geometric domains.

title: Mental-Health Subreddit Classification — An Explanation-Reliability Audit
abstract: This preregistration specifies a confirmatory audit of explanation reliability for a binary mental-health subreddit classification task. The study evaluates SHAP explanations jointly in stability, faithfulness, and calibration across four transformer architectures (BERT-base, RoBERTa-base, MentalBERT, and DistilBERT) and five fixed random seeds, yielding 20 model instances. The study tests whether explanations show above-chance agreement, whether cross-seed variation exceeds the explainer's own estimator noise, whether stability differs across architectures, and whether the composite Explanation Reliability Composite (ERC) provides stronger construct-level association with cross-method explanation agreement than any individual component. Labels are subreddit-derived behavioral proxies and are not clinical diagnoses. The preregistration is filed before confirmatory training; a signed Gate-0 sheet will freeze the remaining implementation parameters before any confirmatory run.

title: Pre-Whitening and BCJR Posterior Distillation for Bi-LSTM Detection in Faster-than-Nyquist Signaling
abstract: Recurrent detectors such as bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) networks are low-complexity alternatives to the optimal Bahl-Cocke-Jelinek-Raviv (BCJR) detector for faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling. Motivated by convolutional detectors that build the intersymbol interference (ISI) structure into their architecture, we ask whether processing nested ISI windows in separate recurrent branches improves the bit error rate (BER) of a Bi-LSTM. Across roughly 260 controlled trainings it does not: at a matched parameter budget and a matched readout, the multi-window architecture never significantly beats a plain Bi-LSTM. Nested windowing is an invertible rearrangement that adds no information, extra branches only add bottlenecks, and a distillation diagnostic shows the network is already near optimal for its window. The limitation is therefore the observation model, not the architecture. Keeping the architecture fixed, we pre-whiten the input, restoring the conditional independence that colored matched-filter noise violates, and distill the BCJR soft posterior into the network. With 3.4% more parameters this reaches 1.05 times the BCJR BER at a compression factor of 0.8 and 1.89 times at 0.7, improving to 1.47 times when the whitened window is widened. The 23.7% BER reduction at 0.8 requires an ill-conditioned ISI matrix but is not monotone in the conditioning, and it holds across five independent noise realizations and a symbol-level McNemar test.

title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Symbol Spotting in Historical Encrypted Manuscripts
abstract: The decipherment of historical encrypted manuscripts poses a fundamental challenge in Digital Humanities: before any transcription can begin, the symbol inventory of the underlying cipher alphabet must first be identified and characterized. We address this challenge through symbol spotting: given a candidate alphabet specified as a set of rendered font glyphs, the task is to determine whether and where its characters appear in an unseen handwritten document, without any labeled examples from the target script. The main difficulty lies in the domain gap between clean, digitally rendered font queries and degraded handwritten manuscript symbols. We propose a three-stage pipeline that bridges this gap without manual annotation, combining a joint SimCLR+DANN encoder for domain-invariant glyph representations with an embedding-space style-adaptation mechanism applied at retrieval time, requiring no re-training. Experiments on fourteen pages from seven encrypted manuscript collections show that our method outperforms zero-shot foundation models, including CLIP and DINOv2, by a large margin ($+0.194$ P@1 over CLIP ViT-L/14), and surpasses task-specific trained baselines by $+0.138$ P@1. We further demonstrate that the Raw-Cover metric, computed in a fully unsupervised setting, provides a meaningful script-family fingerprint that identifies the underlying alphabet of an unknown document. This capability is of direct practical relevance to palaeographers, historians, and other researchers working with undeciphered manuscripts.

We further demonstrate that the Raw-Cover metric, computed in a fully unsupervised setting, provides a meaningful script-family fingerprint that identifies the underlying alphabet of an unknown document. This capability is of direct practical relevance to palaeographers, historians, and other researchers working with undeciphered manuscripts.

title: Single-tone drive-enhanced CROT gate for bosonic quantum error correction
abstract: Bosonic error correction provides a hardware-efficient route to protected qubits for accurate quantum information processing. A critical component for error correction of rotation-symmetric bosonic (RSB) codes, like the well-known cat codes, is the two-mode controlled-rotation (CROT) operation. The CROT gate is useful because of its code-agnostic generality and its error-propagation properties. While the CROT gate can in principle be composed from existing bosonic physical primitives, the desirable properties are typically lost when composed as a sequence of imperfect primitive operations. Past work has focused on direct implementations that rely on features of specific codes. Here, we present a direct route to CROT within the circuit-QED architecture that retains its code-agnostic and error-propagation characteristics. By driving a transmon simultaneously coupled to two microwave cavities, we controllably enhance the effective nonlinearities between the microwave cavities and thus engineer the necessary two-mode interaction underlying the CROT gate. Using only a single drive frequency, we can achieve an on-off ratio sufficient for gate implementation, while minimizing mode distortions. We provide simple analytical formulas that permit the identification of potential working regimes, further refined by exact numerics, and illustrate the efficacy of our CROT approach in an error-correction example involving different RSB codes within the same circuit. Our CROT gate adds to the arsenal of direct two-mode gates available for general bosonic information processing.

title: A visual large language foundational model for medical image recognition using clinician-contributed online resources
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities across diverse domains, showing considerable potential in medicine. However, their application in medical settings remains limited by the scarcity of visual question answering (VQA) datasets that capture clinical reasoning and explicit image-text alignment. Here, we leverage de-identified medical images and expert commentaries shared through clinician-oriented online resources. By combining an advanced LLM with clinician-in-the-loop verification, we established a rigorous pipeline to construct ThoughtMed-1M, a long-form medical VQA dataset containing over one million VQA pairs and designed to capture structured clinical reasoning and medical image-text alignment. To demonstrate its utility, we developed a FOundational LLM Trained on ThoughtMed-1M (FOLTMed). FOLTMed achieved state-of-the-art performance across 42 medical VQA benchmark datasets, with a macro accuracy of 85.4 percent. It also generated more clinically coherent responses on the ThoughtMed-1M test set, outperforming state-of-the-art models by 3 to 5 percent across factuality and similarity metrics, highlighting a scalable paradigm for advancing research on clinically grounded multimodal LLMs.

title: Unraveling the Real Working Mechanism and Inherent Flaws of GAE: A Method for Interpreting Transformer Processes from an Economic Perspective
abstract: We observe a phenomenon that current algorithmic research in the field of explainable artificial intelligence primarily pursues better performance on several proxy metrics. On the one hand, these proxy metrics themselves are more or less flawed and cannot properly measure the quality of methods. On the other hand, metric-oriented research approaches often lead to the neglect of the rationality and interpretability of the methods themselves. Explainable artificial intelligence is abbreviated as XAI. The metric-driven research paradigm has resulted in a lack of interpretability of the relevant XAI methods themselves. Accordingly, there is a need for interpretability research on XAI methods, which can be playfully referred to as XXAI. This paper is one of our works on XXAI. This paper takes Generic Attention-model Explainability (GAE), a widely influential model interpretation method , or rather, XAI method that represents an important technical route, as the research object, and explores the real working mechanism and flaws of this method as well as the technical route it represents. Based on the conclusions of this study, it may be necessary to re-examine or verify GAE-related methods and their domain applications. We argue that GAE is an interpretation method that focuses on the attention process. After pointing out the working mechanism and flaws of GAE, we propose Cumulative Asset Holdings (CAH), a more reasonable Transformer interpretation method integrating both process-based and feature-based ideas from an economic zero-sum games perspective. In addition, it is worth noting that our method is applicable to models with special tokens, where existing methods may suffer from limitations. The model simplification research method and the analysis of additive operations adopted in this study may provide inspiration for other research works in XAI.

title: LLM Layers Immediately Correct Each Other
abstract: Recent methods in language model interpretability employ techniques such as sparse autoencoders to decompose residual stream contributions into linear, semantically meaningful features. Such methods are commonly interpreted as identifying features that persist in the residual stream and that subsequent layers build upon. We challenge this view by identifying the Transformer Layer Correction Mechanism (TLCM), wherein adjacent transformer layers systematically counteract portions of each other's contributions. TLCM appears in 5 out of 7 major open-source model families and activates across nearly all tokens in diverse texts. We show that TLCM emerges during pretraining, operates most strongly on contextually dependent tokens, and adaptively calibrates its correction strength based on the preceding layer's output. Using the layer Jacobian, we further show that TLCM selectively corrects specific subspaces while reinforcing others, which we interpret through a ``propose-and-reject'' framework in which layers propose candidate features and subsequent layers selectively remove inappropriate ones. This dynamic suggests that the residual stream at any layer contains transient proposals alongside persistent features, helping explain why SAE feature descriptions often have low specificity, why effective model steering requires extreme feature amplification, and why transcoders hold a theoretical advantage over SAEs.

title: MEMOBench: A Process Level Memory Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires acting on information that is no longer visible, yet Vision-Language-Action policies are usually evaluated when the current observation largely determines the next action. Existing robotic memory benchmarks expose this gap, but they still rely mainly on final task success and therefore conflate forgetting with manipulation failure. We present \textbf{MEMOBench}, a benchmark for process level memory evaluation in robotic manipulation. MEMOBench includes 30 history dependent tasks, 1{,}500 expert demonstrations, and 4{,}200 executable checkpoint instances from 84 templates. Each checkpoint pairs coarse to fine language with a simulator predicate and labels one memory operation: Storage, Update, or Compression. These annotations define Memory Storage Rate, Memory Update Rate, and Memory Compression Rate, which measure memory fidelity alongside task success. Across standard and memory augmented VLA policies, the strongest memory module baseline reaches only 31.9\% average success rate, and high storage often coexists with weak update and compression. Checkpoint language also supervises semantic, contrastive, and framewise memory alignment objectives, yielding modest gains across different memory operations. MEMOBench provides a diagnostic evaluation suite and training supervision for memory grounded robotic policies. The project page is available at https://github.com/Collab-Gen/MEMOBench.

title: Open Tabular Insight Extraction: Where Do We Stand, and Where Should We Go?
abstract: Democratizing access to the knowledge held in large corpora of tables such as data lakes is emerging as a central research challenge. Research in this space is advancing and broadening in scope, increasingly supplying the components to satisfy a person's insight need end-to-end. Yet these efforts remain fragmented across communities that frame the problem under their own conventions, such as table question answering, text-to-SQL, and data analysis agents, with works six times as likely to cite within the same task label as across labels. To bring these communities onto common ground, we establish a holistic framework for this pursuit, which we refer to as Open Tabular Insight Extraction (OpenTI). We formalize OpenTI from first principles around the analytical knowledge a person needs, the procedure for deriving it from a corpus of tables, and how well a result serves the person who sought it. In doing so we consolidate frameworks and terminology across information retrieval, natural language processing, machine learning, databases, and human-computer interaction, and apply this grounding in a systematic review and analysis of systems and benchmarks that work towards OpenTI. We find that current systems do not cover the end-to-end scope of OpenTI, mainly focusing on the analysis itself, and that benchmarks are largely unfit for evaluations in an open setting as inputs presuppose knowledge of tables, and validation mechanisms do not match the setup. Finally, we distill a research agenda towards OpenTI systems, evaluation, and interaction paradigms that surface the insights users need. An interactive companion to our paper is available at https://open-tabular-insight-extraction.github.io.

title: MCP Monoculture: The Systemic Security Failure of Agentic AI Infrastructure
abstract: RS-2026-065. Synthesis of Red Specter's TRUTH SURFACE series — nine architecture analyses of the top AI security vendors — revealing MCP (Model Context Protocol) exposure as a critical vulnerability in every paper. Documents five protocol-level vulnerabilities, eight active CVEs mapped to NIGHTFALL attack classes, and supply chain risks across 973 MCP packages. Calls on the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation for protocol reform. The central finding: every vendor is vulnerable because the protocol is vulnerable. Cites TRUTH SURFACE #001-#009, RS-2026-063, RS-2026-064. Tool: T287 SPECTER MCP-SCAN v1.0.0.

title: Title: Emergent Pattern Recognition in Multi-Layered Cognitive Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the emergence of complex cognitive patterns within multi-layered neural networks through the development of a novel 'hierarchical coherence' algorithm. Traditional approaches often rely on feature extraction and statistical analysis, failing to capture the dynamic interplay of information across multiple layers. This work proposes a method that analyzes the propagation of patterns, quantifying interdependence to identify emergent cognitive structures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulated and experimental analyses, revealing a significant shift from passive feature representation to active pattern formation. The core mechanism centers on a hierarchical coherence algorithm that progresses through multiple layers, quantifying the degree of interdependence and identifying key nodes that drive pattern evolution. This offers a more holistic and insightful approach to understanding the underlying dynamics of cognition within complex neural systems.

title: 基于动态拓扑的概率分布建模
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic topology as a framework for probabilistic model construction. Traditional probabilistic modeling often relies on static assumptions and limited flexibility. We propose a novel method leveraging dynamic topology, allowing for the adaptive adjustment of probability distribution parameters through a process of topology manipulation. This approach offers a significant advantage in modeling complex, non-linear probability distributions, facilitating parameter optimization and enhanced model generalization. The core mechanism involves the construction of a dynamic topology, which iteratively adjusts parameters to achieve a desired probabilistic outcome. The paper presents a theoretical foundation for this dynamic topology approach and provides a practical implementation utilizing a specific algorithm for parameter optimization. We explore the benefits of this method in various scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing complex dependencies within probability distributions.

title: The Implicit Information Space
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for automated reasoning and learning, centered around the concept of an Implicit Information Space. We propose a method leveraging the inherent relationships within variables and the dynamic nature of information flow to enable robust and adaptable knowledge representation. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating this space, facilitating automated inference and knowledge graph construction. The significance of this approach lies in its potential to overcome limitations of traditional knowledge graph approaches, offering increased autonomy and adaptability to complex systems. This research investigates the design and implementation of this framework, highlighting its advantages and potential applications across diverse domains.

title: 基于多尺度信息检索的自适应知识图谱构建
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to constructing adaptive knowledge graphs (KGs) based on multi-scale information retrieval. The core claim is that by leveraging multi-scale information retrieval, combining knowledge entities and relationships at different granularities, the knowledge graph construction process can be adaptively optimized, leading to improved KG quality and scalability. The proposed mechanism decomposes KG construction into multi-scale information retrieval stages. At low scales, precise matching is the primary goal, retrieving fragments highly related to existing entities and relationships. At high scales, conceptual association is the focus, retrieving fragments with potential associations. The results of these different-scale retrievals are then fused and filtered to progressively build a more comprehensive and accurate KG. This approach addresses limitations of existing KG construction methods that often rely on predefined rules or manual intervention, offering an adaptive solution to reduce noise and uncertainty. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of retrieval strategies based on the evolving KG structure. This work aims to provide a robust and scalable method for KG construction, particularly in scenarios with incomplete or noisy data. The proposed framework utilizes a hierarchical approach to information retrieval, allowing for a nuanced understanding of relationships within a knowledge domain. The methodology is presented with a focus on the algorithmic design and the integration of different retrieval techniques. title: Title: Non-Euclidean Topology for Quantum State Encoding
abstract: Quantum state encoding is a fundamental challenge in quantum information theory, demanding novel approaches to maintain quantum coherence. This paper investigates the application of non-Euclidean topology as a potential tool for achieving this goal. We propose a method for representing quantum states using a non-Euclidean space, exploiting its inherent properties for enhanced quantum coherence. The core mechanism centers around a representation of the quantum state using a non-Euclidean space, leveraging its unique properties for encoding and manipulation. This research explores the implications of this approach, particularly its potential to improve quantum entanglement and information processing. The significance of this work lies in the potential to offer a fundamentally new paradigm for quantum state management, driven by the intersection of topology and quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Computing Accelerated Non-Linear Model Simulation
abstract: Quantum Computing Accelerated Non-Linear Model Simulation presents a novel approach to accelerating computationally intensive non-linear model simulations. This research explores the utilization of quantum computing's unique properties, specifically superposition and entanglement, to enhance the simulation of complex physical phenomena. The core mechanism involves leveraging these quantum features to overcome the limitations of classical computational methods, offering the potential for significant speedups in simulation times and the ability to tackle problems currently intractable with conventional approaches. This paper details the design of a framework integrating quantum algorithms and simulation techniques to achieve this acceleration. We present initial results demonstrating the feasibility of this approach, focusing on a specific example – the simulation of a quantum fluid – highlighting the benefits and challenges of this emerging field. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of this technology on diverse scientific and engineering applications.

title: 基于动态拓扑的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their effectiveness in complex, non-linear scenarios. We propose a framework that utilizes dynamic topology to dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on the input data's geometric structure. The core innovation lies in a quantum-inspired mapping mechanism that transforms optimization parameters into a dynamic topology, enabling the algorithm to adapt to varying input data characteristics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing improved efficiency and robustness compared to existing static optimization techniques. The proposed algorithm offers a significant advancement in optimization by incorporating a self-adapting topology, which leads to more efficient and reliable solutions.

title: Information Flow Dynamics Model for Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper proposes the Information Flow Dynamics Model (IFDM), a novel framework for understanding and analyzing the training process of neural networks. The core claim is that neural network training can be accurately described as an information flow dynamics process. This model utilizes information flow dynamics equations to represent and analyze the movement and exchange of information within a neural network during training. Unlike traditional approaches that primarily focus on gradient descent and optimization algorithms, IFDM offers a fundamentally different perspective by treating the training process as a continuous flow of information governed by specific dynamics. This approach allows for a more intuitive and potentially more powerful understanding of the underlying mechanisms driving neural network learning. The model is presented with detailed equations and explores key concepts such as information entropy, information flux, and network connectivity. ---

title: Non-Linear Differential Equation Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic Gaussian theory to the modeling of non-linear differential equations. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on observed data, enabling automatic feature learning and improved simulation accuracy. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically generated "generalized function" representing the solution to the differential equation, allowing the model to adapt to complex data characteristics. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement over traditional methods, reducing the need for manual parameter tuning and facilitating more accurate and robust simulations in various scientific domains.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Quantum Circuit Simulation with Adaptive Precision
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum circuit simulation leveraging probabilistic programming and adaptive precision. Traditional quantum simulation methods often struggle with scalability and accuracy, particularly when dealing with complex circuits and noisy environments. Our framework addresses these challenges by dynamically adjusting the computational precision employed during simulation, focusing resources on areas exhibiting the highest uncertainty in the quantum state. We utilize a stochastic variational approach within a probabilistic programming environment, allowing for an iterative refinement of the simulation's accuracy. This adaptive strategy significantly improves efficiency and accuracy compared to fixed-precision simulations. The core claim is that this combination enables efficient quantum circuit simulation by dynamically adjusting computational precision based on the uncertainty of the quantum state. This research presents a new paradigm for quantum simulation, offering potential for broader application and improved performance.

title: 基于动态量子态的拓扑信息编码
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum information encoding utilizing dynamic quantum states and topological structure. Traditional encoding methods often rely on manipulating individual quantum states, while this method leverages the inherent properties of topological quantum systems to encode information. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the quantum state to achieve high-dimensional quantum states with enhanced encoding and decoding capabilities. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the non-linearity of topological quantum states through quantum entanglement, enabling efficient and robust information transfer. This research explores the potential of this technique for advanced quantum computing and quantum communication applications. We demonstrate the feasibility of encoding and decoding complex quantum states using this framework.

title: Core Claim: We propose a Gaussian Process-driven Self-Organizing Theory, leveraging the adaptive properties of Gaussian Processes to combine mathematical self-organization with dynamic system structure modeling, particularly in dynamic systems modeling.
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Gaussian Process-based Self-Organizing Theory designed to enhance the modeling and optimization of complex systems, with a focus on dynamic system modeling. The core of this theory lies in a dynamically adaptive 'jump' mechanism within the Gaussian Process, enabling the system to adjust its self-organization based on system dynamics and initial conditions. This approach provides a fundamentally new perspective on modeling self-organization, moving beyond static self-organization parameters to a dynamic and adaptive process. We explore the design of this jump mechanism, its impact on model prediction and optimization, and its potential for more accurate system representation. The theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in modeling complex, dynamic systems. title: Topological Quantum Information Encoding (TQI)
abstract: This paper introduces the Topological Quantum Information Encoding (TQI) method, a novel approach to quantum information processing focused on leveraging the inherent topological properties of quantum states. Traditional methods often struggle with the limitations of qubit entanglement and the difficulty in efficiently encoding and transmitting complex quantum information. TQI addresses these challenges by employing a structured encoding scheme that utilizes topological quantum states to achieve enhanced storage, transmission, and processing capabilities. The paper details the core mechanism of TQI, highlighting its potential to significantly improve the efficiency of quantum information management. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of the TQI method in encoding and manipulating quantum states, showcasing its promise for advancing quantum technologies.

title: A Type-3 Pairing-Based Attribute-Based Encryption Scheme with Expressive Keyword Search and Trapdoor Delegation
abstract: Cloud data sharing allows users to outsource data storage and management to external servers, but it also raises privacy concerns when data must remain encrypted while still supporting efficient search and fine-grained access control. Attribute-based encryption with keyword search (ABE-EKS) addresses this problem by combining searchable encryption with attribute-based access policies. However, existing schemes often focus on separate aspects such as expressive search, online/offline computation, revocation, or policy protection, while controlled trapdoor delegation and inequality-based keyword predicates are less commonly considered together in an implementation-oriented Type-3 pairing setting. This paper revisits the ABE-EKS framework of Yang et al. and adapts it to the Type-3 pairing setting. The construction follows the main structure of Yang et al.’s ABE-EKS scheme, but places the group elements in the appropriate source groups for asymmetric pairings. It further supports expressive access-control and keyword-search policies, Boolean keyword predicates, inequality comparisons, and trapdoor key delegation. We also analyse its security under the honest-but-curious cloud model and implement the scheme using the Apache Milagro Cryptographic Library (AMCL). Experimental results on the Enron Email dataset demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed construction for outsourced encrypted data-sharing scenarios.

title: Depersonalization of personal data in the banking sector: Analysis of methods and selection of an implementation strategy
abstract: This article examines the pressing issue of personal data anonymization in credit and ﬁnancial institutions (CFIs) in the context of tightening regulatory requirements, in particular, Roskomnadzor Order No. 140. It analyzes classic and modern anonymization methods (masking, pseudonymization, synthetic data generation, etc.) for their applicability in a banking environment where preserving data formats, referential integrity, and high performance are critical. A comparative assessment of three modern domestic solutions is provided: DataMask, Garda Data Masking, and N1 AI. Their systemic limitations are identiﬁed, including potential non-compliance with new regulations, insufﬁcient ﬂexibility for unique banking entities, and high cost of ownership. Based on this analysis, the strategic feasibility of developing a specialized internal anonymization tool is substantiated. This tool guarantees full regulatory compliance, maximum adaptability to the bank’s business processes, and long-term economic efﬁciency. A credit and ﬁnancial institution is characterized by processing an extensive array of structured personal data (PD), which combines the features of general, other data, and information that constitutes bank secrecy. This information is typically stored in relational databases in a formalized format (separate ﬁelds for passport number, phone number, account number, etc.), which, on the one hand, simpliﬁes their automated search, but on the other hand, requires strict protection measures, including secure anonymization for use in non-production environments. This determines the key requirements for the system under consideration: the need to accurately detect ﬁelds of various categories of ﬁnancial and identifying information, and the use of masking algorithms that ensure irreversible conversion while preserving the structural integrity and data format for the correct operation of test systems.

title: Comparing supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization for terminology-aware English-to-French medical machine translation
abstract: Die maschinelle Übersetzung im medizinischen Bereich birgt Risiken, die bei Übersetzungen in allgemeinen Bereichen nicht bestehen. Eine flüssige, aber terminologisch falsche Übersetzung kann medizinischem Personal und Patient:innen falsche Informationen vermitteln, und solche Fehler werden leicht übersehen, weil der gesamte Text durch die natürliche Sprache korrekt wirkt. Die genannten Fehler können sogar bis zum Tod führen und unterstreichen, wie wichtig es ist, dieses Thema zu untersuchen und zu erforschen. Die vorliegende Arbeit untersucht, ob Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) die Genauigkeit der medizinischen Terminologieübersetzung bei der maschinellen Übersetzung vom Englischen ins Französische im Vergleich zu Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) allein verbessert. Der Ansatz ist empirisch und vergleichend angelegt, da dieselben Daten und dasselbe Bewertungsverfahren auf drei mehrsprachige Decoder-only-Sprachmodelle angewendet werden, nämlich TowerInstruct-7B, Ministral-8B-Instruct und Qwen3-8B. Jedes Modell wird zunächst mit einem Zero-Shot-Ansatz als Baseline evaluiert und durchläuft anschließend SFT, eine terminologie-angereicherte SFT-Variante und eine terminologie-gestützte DPO-Variante, sodass beobachtete Unterschiede dem jeweils veränderten Schritt zugeschrieben werden können. Die Modelle werden mit Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)-Methoden (QLoRA) auf dem englisch-französischen Parallelkorpus EMEA v3 feinabgestimmt. Dieses Korpus wird durch heuristische und semantische Filter von rund 1,09 Millionen Satzpaaren auf etwa 287.000 reduziert und anschließend in 20.000 Trainings-, 1.000 Validierungs- und 1.000 Testpaare aufgeteilt. Zusätzlich ist der TICO-19-Benchmark vollständig als zentraler Testdatensatz reserviert. Medizinische Begriffe werden aus dem englischen Text mit einem klinischen Named-Entity Recogniser extrahiert und führen über eine Abfrage im Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) zur bevorzugten französischen Übersetzung. Diese Begriffe werden als Glossar in den Instruction Prompt eingefügt und bilden so die mit Terminologie angereicherte SFT-Variante. Für DPO wird zunächst der Adapter in das Basismodell integriert und ein neuer Adapter angehängt. Anschließend werden Präferenzpaare aus acht generierten Hypothesen gebildet und gereiht, wobei die Präferenzstärke über einen Sweep ausgewählt wird. Die Evaluierung kombiniert BLEU, ChrF und COMET mit einer Berechnung der Terminologiegenauigkeit, gepaarten Bootstrap-Signifikanztests und einer manuellen Inspektion der Systemausgaben. Das zentrale Ergebnis ist ein deutlich negatives Resultat für DPO. Über alle drei Modelle und beide Testdatensätze hinweg unterscheidet sich das terminologie-bewusste DPO-System vom terminologie-angereicherten SFT-System höchstens um wenige Tausendstel für COMET, und die Wahl der Präferenzstärke hat wenig Einfluss. Bei Qwen erzeugen das überwachte und das präferenzoptimierte System häufig sehr ähnliche Ausgaben. SFT hat einen größeren Effekt. Im Vergleich zur Zero-Shot-Baseline verbessert es COMET für Tower und Qwen auf dem EMEA-Testset, sinkt jedoch für alle Modelle auf dem TICO-19-Testset unter die Werte der Baseline. Terminologieanreicherung verändert die Werte über beide Testsets hinweg inkonsistent und liefert keine verlässliche Verbesserung. BLEU und ChrF unterscheiden sich von COMET in ihrem Verhalten, was dafür spricht, eine neuronale Metrik für die primäre Messung zu verwenden. Die Arbeit präsentiert reproduzierbare Zero-Shot-, SFT- und DPO-Systeme für die medizinische Englisch-Französisch-Übersetzung sowie die methodischen Schritte, die erforderlich sind, um DPO stabil auf parameter-effizienten Modellen zu trainieren. Die weitergehende Folge ist, dass die Wahl des Basismodells und dessen Stärke für die terminologische Genauigkeit wichtiger sind als die hier untersuchte Präferenzoptimierungsphase und dass verlässliche Genauigkeit in bezug auf die korrekte Terminologieübersetzung wahrscheinlich Mechanismen erfordern wird, die die Verwendung korrekter Begriffe erzwingen, statt sie nur zu suggerieren.

Im Vergleich zur Zero-Shot-Baseline verbessert es COMET für Tower und Qwen auf dem EMEA-Testset, sinkt jedoch für alle Modelle auf dem TICO-19-Testset unter die Werte der Baseline. Terminologieanreicherung verändert die Werte über beide Testsets hinweg inkonsistent und liefert keine verlässliche Verbesserung. BLEU und ChrF unterscheiden sich von COMET in ihrem Verhalten, was dafür spricht, eine neuronale Metrik für die primäre Messung zu verwenden. Die Arbeit präsentiert reproduzierbare Zero-Shot-, SFT- und DPO-Systeme für die medizinische Englisch-Französisch-Übersetzung sowie die methodischen Schritte, die erforderlich sind, um DPO stabil auf parameter-effizienten Modellen zu trainieren. Die weitergehende Folge ist, dass die Wahl des Basismodells und dessen Stärke für die terminologische Genauigkeit wichtiger sind als die hier untersuchte Präferenzoptimierungsphase und dass verlässliche Genauigkeit in bezug auf die korrekte Terminologieübersetzung wahrscheinlich Mechanismen erfordern wird, die die Verwendung korrekter Begriffe erzwingen, statt sie nur zu suggerieren.

title: Decomposition-Guided Diffusion Language Models for Inertial Confinement Fusion Prediction
abstract: Inertial confinement fusion (ICF) is a leading pathway toward clean energy, but each shot at the National Ignition Facility costs on the order of one million dollars, making accurate AI surrogates a high-value target. We study exogenous-driven ICF waveform prediction, where a 512-step neutron-rate diagnostic must be inferred directly from a laser pulse and target design parameters, with no historical response observed. The regime stresses standard time-series predictors with temporal sparsity (picosecond peak in a nanosecond window), input-output scale mismatch (under 300 real shots), and peak sensitivity (picosecond timing). We propose ICF-DLM, to our knowledge the first LM-based ICF predictor, combining (i) a physics-typed decomposition into yield $Y_{DT}$, peak timing $t_{\mathrm{peak}}$, and local waveform $w_{\mathrm{local}}$; (ii) bidirectional denoising that defers commitment to peak location; and (iii) a physics-driven PPO reward re-injecting metric structure across numeric tokens. On ICFBench (50K simulations + 232 experimental shots), ICF-DLM cuts peak-timing error from 11.6 to 9.2 steps over a matched autoregressive LLaMA-3-8B and outperforms classical sequence models and LLM-based time-series predictors. Beyond ICF, the recipe shows potential to address science domains with low data and sparse events.

title: World Models Under Asynchronous Sensor Observations
abstract: Learned world models typically assume that observations arrive synchronously, an abstraction inherited from simulators that return a complete state vector at each environment step. Physical sensing instead operates at heterogeneous rates, leaving most observation channels stale at any given instant. Interpolating stale channels introduces measurements that were never observed, while downsampling to the slowest sensor discards valid measurements. A natural alternative is to zero-order-hold the most recent reading and provide the known sampling schedule to the model through two features, staleness and time-to-refresh. We test this prediction using transformer world models across three regimes of increasing causal coupling: open-loop rollouts in continuous-control locomotion, closed-loop model-predictive planning in which each learned model serves as the planner dynamics, and a linear latched-actuator system in which refresh events apply a zero-order-held command to the plant. Our findings show that the effectiveness of time-to-refresh depends on the causal role of the sampling schedule, specifically when refresh events affect the system rather than merely report its state. These results establish when sampling schedules provide useful information for predictive world models operating under asynchronous physical observations.

title: Design and Development of an Intelligent Multi-Format Document Processing System Using Agentic AI and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Enterprise document workflows still depend heavily on manual review of unstructured technical, contractual, and administrative files, and conventional keyword or OCR-based extraction pipelines fail to preserve layout, tabular structure, and multilingual context. This paper presents an intelligent, self-correcting document processing system that combines layout-aware ingestion with a four-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline. The ingestion stage passes PDF, CSV and TXT documents including automated Gmail/IMAP intake with SHA-256 content deduplication applies sliding-window chunking, and indexes dense embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) in a persistent Chroma vector store. At query time, a Planning, Retrieval, Generation and Compliance/Validation agent graph retrieves the top-k relevant chunks and produces a deterministic, source-grounded answer (Llama-3.3-70B, temperature = 0.0), refusing to respond when grounding is insufficient. On a diagnostic benchmark of ten entity-disambiguation queries over heterogeneous technical documents, the system achieved 100% Recall@6, 100% Correctness, Relevance, and Completeness and a per-criterion Faithfulness score of 60% a discrepancy traced not to factual error but to the LLM-as-a-Judge harness penalizing natural-language phrasing of compact source facts. The findings position agentic, self-correcting RAG as a practical, auditable alternative to single pass pipelines for document heavy Industry 4.0 environments.

title: KJac: Constraint-Aware NAS for Learned Optimization
abstract: This preprint presents KJac, a zero-training neural architecture search proxy for learned optimization in constrained optimization settings. The study evaluates Jacobian-based architecture scoring across linear projection, convex quadratic programming, QCQP-style constraints, and portfolio optimization tasks. It examines predictive correlation with final model performance, computational cost, feasibility-aware diagnostics, and architecture selection behavior. The work investigates the utility and limitations of Jacobian-based proxies for architecture search in constrained learned-optimization problems.

title: NSRDB Datasets for Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI) Forecasting Across India (Madurai), Brazil, and Nepal (2012–2014)
abstract: "This dataset contains the processed and feature-engineered NSRDB meteorological and solar irradiance data (2012–2014) for three climatically distinct locations — Madurai (India), Brazil, and the Himalayas (Nepal) — used to train and evaluate six machine learning models for Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI) forecasting, as reported in Performance Evaluation of Supervised Machine Learning Algorithms for Direct Normal Irradiance Forecasting in Diverse Climatic Conditions. Each location folder contains the training (2012–2013) from raw NSRDB inputs are third-party data and link to nsrdb.nrel.gov.

abstract: Reproducibility package for the Salud Digital ICU mortality prediction study. The package contains analysis scripts, aggregate non-patient-level outputs, variable documentation, execution instructions, environment files, and revised manuscript materials for evaluating intra-domain validation and cross-domain transfer between MIMIC-III Demo and eICU-CRD. Patient-level MIMIC/eICU raw or derived records are not included because the source databases are PhysioNet clinical resources subject to credentialing, data-use agreements, and access controls.

title: Emergent Complexity from Sparse Connectivity in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the potential for sparse connectivity patterns to foster emergent complexity within neural networks, contributing to improved generalization performance. Traditional approaches often treat connectivity as a fixed attribute, neglecting the dynamic evolution driven by training data. We propose a novel framework that dynamically models connectivity changes and quantifies their impact on network representation, focusing on how these patterns influence the network's capacity to learn complex functions. The paper introduces a modified connection matrix approach, incorporating a measure of sparsity and dynamically adjusting connectivity weights based on training data. We demonstrate through a series of experiments that this approach significantly improves performance on benchmark datasets, particularly in tasks requiring robust feature extraction and generalization. The results highlight the importance of considering dynamic connectivity patterns for enhancing neural network capabilities.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation: An Adaptive Quantum Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum algorithm, "Quantum Entanglement Computation," designed to exploit this phenomenon for enhanced quantum computation. The core of this algorithm lies in the introduction of a "Quantum State Adaptation" mechanism, which dynamically adjusts quantum gate parameters based on the inherent evolution of the quantum state. This adaptive approach contrasts with traditional algorithms, which rely on static parameter settings, offering a pathway towards significantly improved computational efficiency. We detail the mechanism, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating its efficacy. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of this adaptive quantum algorithm on the field of quantum computing.

title: Quantum Machine Learning in Adaptive Matrix Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing machine learning algorithms, particularly in areas demanding complex computations. This research investigates a novel approach to QML, specifically focusing on the optimization of matrix operations, aiming to significantly accelerate model training and improve generalization capabilities. We propose a quantum-enhanced matrix optimization technique leveraging the unique properties of quantum machine learning to address the computational bottlenecks inherent in traditional optimization methods. The core mechanism centers around quantum algorithms designed to efficiently navigate and manipulate matrices, leading to faster convergence and enhanced model performance. This work presents a framework for adapting to quantum machine learning, offering a potential pathway to accelerate the training and deployment of complex models.

title: Adaptive Quantum Algorithm-Based Topological Topology Analysis (AQT)
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Quantum Algorithm-Based Topological Topology Analysis (AQT) method, a novel approach to topology analysis that leverages quantum algorithms for rapid identification and optimization of complex topological structures. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and scale of these structures. AQT offers significant improvements in computational efficiency and accuracy through the application of quantum algorithms tailored for topological analysis. This paper details the fundamental principles of AQT, presents a preliminary implementation demonstrating its effectiveness, and discusses potential future developments and applications within the field of topology. The core mechanism of AQT revolves around the quantum-enhanced exploration of topological spaces, enabling the identification of subtle patterns and relationships that would be missed by classical methods.

title: Title: Adaptive Bias-Variance Trade-off via Constraint Propagation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to bias-variance reduction, introducing an adaptive mechanism that dynamically adjusts the model's parameters based on the data's inherent statistical structure. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameters or simplistic regularization, failing to adequately address the complexities of real-world datasets. We propose a framework centered around constraint propagation, which iteratively refines model parameters to minimize errors across different data subsets. The core innovation lies in the algorithm's ability to intelligently identify and exploit the data's underlying patterns, resulting in improved generalization performance. This work addresses a critical limitation of existing techniques by providing a flexible and adaptive solution to the bias-variance trade-off. The proposed method offers a promising path toward more robust and accurate models.
