evidence.title: Guiding Worker Self-Selection in Crowdsourcing Contests: An LLM-Augmented Algorithmic Approach
evidence.abstract: Crowdsourcing platforms coordinate large pools of online workers who strategically choose which contests to enter and how much effort to invest. This self-selection can leave important contests with too few participants or too little effort, while workers may regret entering contests that leave them worse off than available alternatives. We study how platforms can recommend contests to workers using self-selection in Tullock contests (SSTC), a two-stage model in which workers first choose contests and then compete within them. We introduce GRAF, a greedy polynomial-time framework that constructs self-selection outcomes by ordering workers according to a score vector, with guarantees of zero worker regret and platform optimality in special cases of SSTC. Because effective orderings are difficult to design under worker heterogeneity, we propose LLMScore, an LLM-driven evolutionary framework that automatically designs GRAF's scoring algorithm. LLMScore addresses two challenges: jointly optimizing platform utility and worker satisfaction, and evaluating worker regret when exact computation is intractable. Trained only on small instances of one setting, it transfers to larger and structurally different settings; moreover, its output is human-readable code that platform operators can inspect and modify. Across 1,000 synthetic instances spanning four settings, GRAF with LLMScore consistently achieves high-quality, often near-optimal, outcomes with low worker regret, benefiting both platforms and workers.

title: An LLM-Associated Register Shift in Korean Journal Abstracts: A Morphology-Aware Excess-Vocabulary Study, 2018-2026
abstract: Excess vocabulary, a word's frequency above its pre-2023 trend, is how the change in scholarly English after 2022 has been measured. We adapt it to Korean with morphological units on 398,296 KCI abstracts (2018-August 2026), with 47,165 Vietnamese abstracts for comparison. Placebo floors are 0.1-2.2 points for the single-word statistic and at most 2.9 for the re-selected split-half set statistic. Korean abstracts show nothing in 2023, onset in late 2024, a rise through 2025 flattening in mid-2026: sisahada "suggest" appears in 21.4% of 2026 abstracts against 5.3% expected; plain verbs like araboda "look into" fall to a quarter of trend. Under stated assumptions the single-word conditional lower bound on LLM-processed abstracts is 3.5%, 10.5% and 16.1% for 2024-2026 and a split-half set bound 7.8%, 20.6% and 33.0%. Holzwarth et al.'s estimator under the same discipline gives 41.9% and 72.1% for 2025-2026. Subject-matter controls reduce but do not remove it: restricting the set to lemmas three language-model annotators all call style leaves 14.7 of the 33.0 points, and pairing each 2026 abstract with its journal's closest base-period abstract leaves 34.1. Tested translation routes do not explain it: the surface marks of translated Korean fall as the markers rise. In the same articles' English abstracts the excess appears a year earlier; where the English side carries none, the Korean shift persists at 30 to 66% of the rate where it does. Control abstracts from three providers reproduce the rising words, with marker turnover consistent with model generations; implied prevalences are scenario-dependent.

title: Human-agent discovery of reconfigurable in-plane ferroelectric superdomain control
abstract: Automated experimentation is most effective when the observables, available actions, and objective are defined before the experiment starts, as is the case for Bayesian optimization. However, in many exploratory experiments, the variables that describe the sample must be extracted from the data, new operations emerge during the experiments, and the instrument budget is too small to learn the problem by trials. Here we introduce the Scanning Probe Agentic Research Cycle (SPARC) framework, in which a coding agent and a human operator share one microscope, one notebook, and two persistent memory files. FINDINGS.md stores graded conclusions about the experiment, whereas PITFALLS.md records learned failure modes of analysis and instrument. We apply SPARC to reconfigure the in-plane superdomain direction of a (111)-oriented PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 film. In an operator-supervised campaign, the agent reanalyzed earlier manual measurements and developed an oriented lattice of stationary bias pulses with alternating polarity to reconfigure the superdomain direction. In a subsequent agent-controlled campaign, PITFALLS.md entries were compiled into checks that validate a design before any write. The experiments showed that spatial polarity alternation, instead of the exact matching between the lattice and lamellar periods, determines directional selection. Combining a raster scan with a masked pulse lattice printed the letters UTK into the superdomain orientation. The campaign also identified practical requirements for agentic experimentation where physical verification of instrument execution, the conditions under which stored findings remain valid, validation of new observables on instrument data, and robust control protocols.

title: CosmoH2G: A Hand-to-Gripper Transfer Dataset and Baseline Method for Object Manipulation with Complex Spatial Movements
abstract: Transferring human hand demonstrations to robotic grippers has recently emerged as a cost-effective solution for robot learning. However, existing methods are largely confined to simple, planar tasks and fail to handle complex spatial movements (e.g., intricate trajectories involving rotations or flips) that are essential for robot manipulation. Motivated by this gap, we adopt an implicit, data-driven approach guided by fine-grained hand-pose motions. To this end, we introduce a scalable acquisition pipeline to collect hand-gripper paired demonstrations, governed by a rigorous protocol that prioritizes motion complexity and leverages a handheld gripper for seamless action mimicry. This yields a large-scale paired dataset comprising 6,189 episodes across 1,254 unique objects, exhibiting significantly higher spatial complexity than existing benchmarks. However, learning such complex mappings remains challenging. We observe that naive end-to-end generation of full gripper pose sequences is insufficient, as minor trajectory deviations compound rapidly under intricate dynamics. To address this, we propose a two-stage framework: Stage I predicts sparse gripper keyframes (initial and terminal) to simplify the mapping objective, while Stage II generates the full continuous action sequence conditioned on these keyframes. Furthermore, to mitigate cumulative drift, we keep the gripper's orientation being learned while post-optimizing its translation based on the grasping heuristic and kinematic consistency. In both simulation and real-robot experiments, our framework enables stable and precise hand-to-gripper transfer of complex spatial manipulations, significantly outperforming traditional baselines. Project page: https://cosmoh2g.github.io.

title: CSN Quantum Computing Processes in the Human Brain
abstract: CSN stands for Catalin Silviu Nutu, and it is the acronym for the name of the author who has developed the theory related to the CSN Algorithm, such as presented in his previous work published so far. Current conventional and classical AI models today, mainly based on supervised and unsupervised learning, have almost reached their limits, and they are completely insufficient and totally inadequate to simulate and to model highly sophisticated and complicated brain processes involved in highly creative and extremely innovative brain processes. Based on the theory introduced, developed and presented by the author related to the CSN Algorithm and by introducing a new type of special matrix named CSN Matrix of Activations, this paper generates a quantum computing model named CSN Quantum Computing brain model. This paper expands on the latest work of the author presented in his last papers on this topic, namely “Decryption of Evolutionary Fractals by means of Procedural Randomness generated with an Intelligence Model based on the CSN Algorithm”, presented at the International Conference XR Salento 2025 in Otranto, Italy, and a subsequent paper entitled “Enhanced Intelligence Models based on the CSN Algorithm”, also published in 2025, in the International Journal of Computational Engineering Research (IJCER)

title: Executable Matrix-Product Unitaries: A Geometric Operator Framework for Quantum Circuits
abstract: Quantum circuit theory has long treated Matrix‑Product Unitaries (MPUs) as elegant but unreachable objects—beautiful on paper, impossible to extract, and as far as we know never once executed on real hardware. This work breaks that barrier. We introduce the first geometric MPU extraction pipeline capable of reconstructing full multi‑qubit unitaries with machine‑precision fidelity, validating them across uniform CZ layers, bidirectional sweeps, non‑uniform constructions, QFT‑derived operators, high‑bond entangling layers, and multi‑layer MPU compositions. Every MPU class tested—without exception—compiles cleanly through Qiskit into hardware‑native CX+U3 circuits, producing thousands‑gate decompositions that match the original MPU operators with Frobenius error near 10^{-11} and fidelity 1.0. For the first time, MPUs move from abstract tensor‑network theory into executable quantum computation. This establishes a practical bridge between MPU mathematics and real quantum devices, opening a new path for hardware‑compatible tensor‑network operators, circuit compression, and quantum algorithm design.

title: Dynamic Probability Graphs: Modeling and Optimization of Complex Systems
abstract: Dynamic Probability Graphs (DPGs) represent a novel approach to modeling complex systems by dynamically updating graph structures based on real-time environmental changes. This paper introduces a method employing reinforcement learning and evolutionary algorithms to optimize the graph structure, ensuring model predictability and accurate system behavior prediction. The core mechanism focuses on a continuous adjustment process, dynamically responding to evolving conditions. Traditional approaches often suffer from static models, failing to capture the dynamic nature of real-world systems. This research addresses this limitation by creating a flexible and adaptive representation, offering improved predictive capabilities and optimization potential.

title: Adaptive Dynamic Probability Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for probabilistic modeling, termed the Adaptive Dynamic Probability Model (ADPM), that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on data. The core innovation lies in a self-adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism, enabling the model to continuously optimize its predictive accuracy. This approach contrasts with static probabilistic models, offering increased efficiency and adaptability. We detail the framework's architecture, explain the self-adjustment process, and demonstrate its efficacy through illustrative examples, highlighting its potential for improved predictive performance across various applications.

title: 基于动态自适应的机器学习优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning optimization algorithm, termed "Dynamic Adaptive Learning," designed to enhance predictive accuracy by dynamically adjusting model parameters based on feedback and error. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual design, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. This algorithm leverages a dynamic "Learning Parameter" mechanism that adapts to data and model discrepancy, resulting in improved performance across diverse datasets. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop, allowing the algorithm to refine its parameters in real-time, offering a significant advantage for complex, evolving datasets. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in various scenarios, including high-dimensional data and non-linear relationships.

title: Dynamic Geometric Transformations and Quantum Spin Effects
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of dynamic geometric transformations on quantum spin effects, proposing a novel quantum spin computation framework leveraging the unique quantum properties of spin. We aim to predict and control the evolution of dynamic geometric transformations, ultimately enabling high-precision quantum calculations. The core mechanism centers around utilizing spin's quantum nature to guide and manipulate geometric configurations, providing a fundamentally new approach to quantum computation. This work addresses the limitations of existing static models by introducing a dynamic, self-correcting framework optimized for spin-based calculations. The research highlights the potential of this approach to significantly advance the field of quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Error Correction: Adaptive Synchronization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum computation, enabling the reliable manipulation of quantum states. Current synchronization algorithms, however, often struggle to maintain the required accuracy and speed, particularly in the face of environmental noise. This paper introduces a novel adaptive synchronization algorithm based on quantum error correction principles. The core mechanism leverages the dynamic adjustment of quantum states during the error correction process to achieve higher precision and faster computation, effectively mitigating the impact of noise. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, showcasing its potential to significantly improve the performance of quantum processors. Keywords: Quantum Error Correction, Adaptive Synchronization, Quantum State Synchronization, Quantum Computation, Noise Mitigation.

title: Quantum-Guided Constraint Optimization (QGCO)
abstract: Quantum-Guided Constraint Optimization (QGCO) presents a novel approach to solving complex optimization problems by integrating quantum annealing with constraint optimization techniques. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum annealing to accelerate the search process while simultaneously enforcing constraints, resulting in enhanced solution quality. We delve into the theoretical framework, algorithmic implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this method. The core claim focuses on the synergistic combination of quantum annealing and constraint optimization to achieve a significant improvement in optimization speed and solution quality compared to traditional methods. This research addresses limitations of existing techniques by providing a robust and efficient framework for tackling challenging optimization problems across diverse domains.

title: Nonlinear Matrix Dynamics and Quantum Entanglement: A Theoretical Framework
abstract: This paper explores the potential synergy between nonlinear matrix dynamics and quantum entanglement, aiming to develop a novel matrix operation method based on dynamic conjugation. We investigate how incorporating quantum entanglement into the matrix transformation process could lead to enhanced computational efficiency and reveal novel implications for quantum computation and machine learning. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a dynamic equilibrium between the matrix's inherent linearity and the entangled state, ultimately aiming to unlock new algorithmic possibilities. This research investigates the potential for entanglement to influence the behavior of matrix operations, offering a theoretical foundation for future advancements in these fields.

title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning via Contrastive Relational Embedding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-supervised representation learning approach for graph data, termed Contrastive Relational Embedding. The core challenge in leveraging graphs for machine learning lies in effectively capturing the intricate relationships between nodes. Existing self-supervised methods often fall short in this regard, primarily focusing on unsupervised node embeddings without explicitly considering the relational context. Our method addresses this limitation by training a neural network to learn embeddings that reflect the underlying graph structure through a contrastive learning framework. Specifically, we define relationships as 'neighbor' and 'connected-to' and use a contrastive loss to pull together embeddings of nodes that share these relations, while pushing apart the embeddings of nodes with different relations. This approach allows the model to learn rich, graph-aware representations without relying on manual annotations. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline, highlighting its potential for improved performance in downstream graph-related tasks.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BREAST CANCER SCREENING: A REVIEW
authors: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BREAST CANCER SCREENING: A REVIEW
abstract: Abstract Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer among women worldwide, and early detection through screening remains essential for reducing mortality. Mammography is the standard screening modality; however, its diagnostic performance may be affected by false positive results, false-negative findings, reduced sensitivity in dense breast tissue, and variability in image interpretation. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning and deep learning, have enhanced breast cancer screening by improving lesion detection, image classification, risk prediction, and workflow efficiency. AI has been successfully applied to mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging, demonstrating promising improvements in diagnostic accuracy and screening performance. Despite these advances, challenges such as limited dataset diversity, algorithm bias, lack of interpretability, regulatory concerns, data privacy, and integration into clinical practice remain barriers to widespread implementation. Ongoing research focusing on robust validation, ethical AI development, and multidisciplinary collaboration is expected to facilitate the safe and effective adoption of AI in breast cancer screening. This review summarizes current applications of AI in breast cancer screening, highlights its clinical benefits and limitations, and discusses future perspectives for integrating AI into evidence-based and personalized breast cancer screening programs.

authors: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BREAST CANCER SCREENING: A REVIEW
evidence.abstract: Abstract Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer among women worldwide, and early detection through screening remains essential for reducing mortality. Mammography is the standard screening modality; however, its diagnostic performance may be affected by false positive results, false-negative findings, reduced sensitivity in dense breast tissue, and variability in image interpretation. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning and deep learning, have enhanced breast cancer screening by improving lesion detection, image classification, risk prediction, and workflow efficiency. AI has been successfully applied to mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging, demonstrating promising improvements in diagnostic accuracy and screening performance. Despite these advances, challenges such as limited dataset diversity, algorithm bias, lack of interpretability, regulatory concerns, data privacy, and integration into clinical practice remain barriers to widespread implementation. Ongoing research focusing on robust validation, ethical AI development, and multidisciplinary collaboration is expected to facilitate the safe and effective adoption of AI in breast cancer screening. This review summarizes current applications of AI in breast cancer screening, highlights its clinical benefits and limitations, and discusses future perspectives for integrating AI into evidence-based and personalized breast cancer screening programs.

title: Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Weaving
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum entanglement weaving algorithm that dynamically constructs and adjusts quantum entanglement networks for improved quantum communication and quantum computation. Traditional entanglement weaving methods are often static, limiting efficiency. Our algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to adjust the size and structure of entangled networks in response to specific requirements, offering a significant advancement over existing approaches. We explore the core mechanism of this dynamic adjustment through a novel control strategy. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to enhance quantum communication and quantum computation through adaptive network design.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement: Distributed Coprocessor
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for distributed coprocessor networks leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to utilize entangled nodes for ultra-fast, secure data transmission and computation, overcoming the limitations of traditional distributed computing systems. We detail a mechanism for constructing a network of entangled nodes, employing entanglement-based measurements and manipulations to facilitate data exchange and computation. The use of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols ensures the security of the communication channel. This approach offers a significant advancement over conventional methods, providing enhanced bandwidth, improved security, and the potential for distributed computing capabilities across extended distances. The theoretical framework and underlying principles are presented, outlining a pathway toward realizing a quantum-enhanced distributed coprocessor network.

title: Adaptive Topological Transformation Algorithm for Quantum Computing (ATTC)
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Topological Transformation Algorithm (ATTC) for quantum computing, designed to dynamically manipulate quantum states. Traditional quantum computation often relies on static state representations, limiting the ability to precisely simulate quantum system behavior. The ATTC leverages topological transformations, a powerful tool in quantum geometry, to optimize quantum states for enhanced efficiency and robustness. This algorithm dynamically adjusts the quantum state structure during a transformation process, resulting in improved performance metrics. The core mechanism focuses on optimizing the quantum state's geometry through a series of carefully designed topological operations. This innovation promises to significantly improve the capabilities of quantum algorithms, particularly in areas requiring precise modeling and dynamic adaptation. We present a comprehensive analysis of the ATTC's design and performance, demonstrating its potential to advance quantum computing paradigms.

title: Non-Standard Probability Model Based on Gaussian Distribution for Adaptive Inference
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-standard probability model predicated on the Gaussian distribution, designed for adaptive inference. The model's core innovation lies in its ability to dynamically adjust inference parameters based on the input data's characteristics, providing a more intelligent and robust reasoning process. Traditional probability models often suffer from fixed parameterization, limiting their effectiveness in complex scenarios. We propose a new framework utilizing a Gaussian distribution to model data dependencies, enabling the model to adjust its inference process in real-time. The proposed method offers improved accuracy and adaptability compared to existing approaches. This work represents a significant step towards creating more intelligent and efficient inference systems.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction with Graph Theory
abstract: Abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computation to revolutionize the field of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs). We propose a novel quantum algorithm designed to accelerate the search for solutions in CSPs by integrating graph theory and quantum superposition. The core mechanism relies on representing the CSP graph as a quantum state and employing superposition to efficiently explore multiple solution paths concurrently. This approach promises significant speedups compared to classical approaches, particularly for large and complex CSPs. The paper details the algorithm's design, potential benefits, and preliminary results demonstrating improved performance.

title: Support Vector Machines for Classification, Regression, and Outlier Detection: A Tutorial
abstract: Support Vector Machine (SVM) is a fundamental machine learning method based on the principle of maximum-margin learning. This chapter develops SVM from its geometric intuition to its optimization formulation and extensions. We first contrast SVM with the Perceptron and motivate the use of the maximum-margin decision boundary. We then derive hard-margin SVM, including the primal and dual optimization problems, the role of Lagrange multipliers, the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) conditions, and the interpretation of support vectors. Soft-margin SVM is subsequently introduced to handle approximately linearly separable data through slack variables and regularization. For nonlinear classification, kernelization and the kernel trick are presented, leading to kernel SVM in which inner products are replaced by kernel evaluations in a possibly high-dimensional feature space. The chapter then extends the support-vector framework beyond classification to Support Vector Regression (SVR), where an $\varepsilon$-insensitive tube is used for regression, and to one-class SVM, where a separating boundary is learned for novelty and outlier detection. Throughout the chapter, emphasis is placed on the connections between geometry, convex optimization, duality, KKT conditions, sparsity, and the role of support vectors across the different formulations.

title: Natural Language Processing for Human–Computer Interaction
abstract: In this work we propose an advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) framework for HCI that handles some of the important challenges such as multilingualism, emotional intelligence, context preservation, and explainability. Utilising transformer-based models, memory-augmented networks, and privacy-preserving learning, the system guarantees robust, adaptive and empathetic interaction in any domain. It allows real-time conversation, cross-domain understanding, and dynamic behavior modeling, without compromising data privacy. The proposed framework also focuses on the scalability, standard evaluation protocols, and ethical compliance for commercialization, which drive it to be a versatile, secure, and unified platform that enable large-scale deployment in next-genre HCI systems.

title: Scaling Multi-Agent Systems with Prospect-State Propagation
abstract: Current LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) periodically compress intermediate states to reduce inference-time token consumption, thereby attempting to incorporate more agents. However, naive scaling strategies face challenges. For example, in economic simulations, large-scale MAS typically discard semantically rich economic states, i.e., agent behavioral trajectories, which are key drivers of macroeconomic fluctuations. In this paper, we reveal a phenomenon in which agent heterogeneity gradually decreases during simulation, and propose Prospect-State Propagation for Multi-Agent Systems (PspMAS). Inspired by prospect theory, PspMAS decouples each agent's micro state into a compact Prospect State and an expressive Semantic State. The former records psychological traces through a lightweight, parallelizable propagator and continuously injects heterogeneity into the system. The latter leverages the strong perception, reasoning, planning, and decision-making abilities of LLMs. These two components work complementarily, providing a scalable LLM-based multi-agent simulation solution.

title: An Empirical Measurement of Jailbreaking Evaluators
abstract: Expert evaluation of jailbreak responses is costly and difficult to scale, so the community increasingly relies on automated evaluators to determine whether an attack succeeds. However, jailbreak studies typically validate their chosen evaluator independently, repeatedly spending resources on similar evaluation efforts while making results across papers difficult to compare. Different evaluators also encode different definitions of jailbreak success, meaning that reported attack strength and apparent progress can depend substantially on which evaluator is used. We systematically compare six evaluators that recur in recent jailbreak attack and defense research: HarmBench, JailbreakBench, JailbreakRadar, StrongReject, JADES, and JailMeter. To our knowledge, no prior study has evaluated all six on the same human-labeled data under a controlled setup. We evaluate them on JailbreakQR and JailMeter-Eva, using human judgments as the reference, and measure agreement with humans, error types, and consistency across attack families. For evaluators that require a general-purpose LLM judge, we use a shared backbone to control for model-specific variation. We found that JADES exhibits the best overall performance, while HarmBench and StrongReject also demonstrate good performance.

title: Train Overcomplete, Deploy Compact: Scaling Recovery Capacity for Structured LLM Pruning
abstract: Large language models achieve strong performance across diverse tasks, but deployment remains costly because of memory, latency, and energy demands. Structured pruning reduces these costs by removing architectural components, yet its recovery stage is often limited by a mismatch between the recovery module's representational capacity and the complexity of the removed knowledge. We call this bottleneck the capacity-knowledge asymmetry and propose OverRep, an Overcomplete Reparameterization framework for structured LLM pruning. Following the principle of "train overcomplete, deploy compact", OverRep temporarily overparameterizes the recovery module during training to absorb complex knowledge distilled from the original model. After recovery, the overcomplete re-parameterization is algebraically merged into a mathematically equivalent compact module, preserving the pruned model's inference-time architecture and computational cost. OverRep further introduces an annealed activation that enables nonlinear training dynamics while converging to a linear regime for exact algebraic merging. Across three backbone families, OverRep improves retained reasoning performance over strong recovery baselines by up to 5.5 and 8.4 points at 25% and 50% pruning, respectively, while keeping memory usage and TFLOPs comparable to existing recovery methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/mmai-laboratory/OverRep.

title: Computing with logarithmicstate and history
abstract: A computation can return to its original state while retaining a nonzero history of interaction. We presentthe application of exact logarithmic state/history in the Substrate Ledger Computer, implemented in SLC-GEN2-R4. Positive source-action ratios become additive coordinates, while their ordered incrementsretain cumulative rise, fall, variation and maximum excursion. These readouts distinguish an unchangedendpoint from an executed loop and recover a historical contact barrier from its logarithmic maximumand original action. An exact composition law joins history segments without changing their referenceor losing maximizing states. The same runtime represents uncertainty over complete linked histories anduses rationally weighted formal logarithms to select native probes and report resolution for a specifiedhistorical target. A four-history receiver example separates equal quantities of source information withdifferent barrier content. Adaptive two-observation policies then resolve a target with an expected 1.5readings while retaining unresolved histories, and a separate lookahead example gains information onlyafter a second interaction. Source-defined scale-and-turn coordinates, quarter-turn golden scheduling,construction-boundary information and signed contribution arithmetic share these contracts. Installedapplications connect the representation to isotope assemblies, exact frustrated-spin spectra and signedMöbius-moment calculations. The resulting method makes logarithmic history an executable object: itcan be queried, composed, used to choose an observation and continued from a complete checkpoint.Keywords: logarithmic computation; executable history; exact arithmetic; conditional reconstruction;adaptive observation; Substrate Ledger Computer

title: 基于非线性模型的量子算法设计
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm design approach leveraging non-linear models. Traditional quantum algorithm design relies heavily on classical optimization techniques, limiting the applicability of quantum computation to specific problem domains. We propose a new method that dynamically adjusts the problem's structure through a non-linear model, enabling the creation of highly efficient quantum algorithms tailored to particular computational challenges. This approach systematically transforms a complex problem into a simplified, solvable optimization problem, facilitating the development of quantum solutions that surpass the capabilities of traditional methods. The core mechanism involves constructing a non-linear model that governs the problem's evolution, allowing for the implementation of quantum circuits that exploit specific properties. This research explores the potential of this technique to unlock new avenues in quantum algorithm development and provide a foundation for more efficient quantum computation.

title: Pulse Geometry Quantum Entanglement Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum entanglement simulation framework, the "Pulse Geometry" model, designed to accurately predict complex quantum systems. Traditional quantum simulation often struggles with the inherent challenges of representing and simulating quantum phenomena, particularly when dealing with intricate entanglement dynamics. The Pulse Geometry framework leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to significantly enhance simulation accuracy and precision. This work proposes a new approach to quantum simulation by utilizing a specially crafted geometric representation of quantum states, intrinsically linked to entanglement, to reduce computational complexity and enhance fidelity. The core mechanism involves creating a dynamic, multi-layered representation of the quantum system, where entanglement is the primary driving force behind its behavior. This is achieved through a unique algorithm that effectively encodes and manipulates entanglement across the system's geometry. The resulting simulation will offer a significant advancement over existing quantum simulation techniques, particularly in the modeling of systems exhibiting strong entanglement.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel optimization algorithm based on the principles of chaos theory to discover and optimize complex systems. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent self-organization exhibited by chaotic systems to automatically identify and refine optimal solutions. Existing optimization techniques often rely on deterministic approaches, limiting their effectiveness in complex scenarios. title: Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning Model Gradient Descent Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic adaptive machine learning model gradient descent optimization method designed to enhance model performance through dynamic adjustment of the gradient descent strategy. Traditional gradient descent methods are often static, limiting their effectiveness in complex, dynamic datasets. This research proposes a novel approach that dynamically adjusts the gradient descent parameters based on the data distribution, leading to improved convergence and generalization. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors the gradient landscape and adjusts the learning rate and step size, effectively adapting to the data's inherent variability. This adaptation significantly improves the model's robustness and generalization capabilities.

abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) is a rapidly developing field with the potential to revolutionize various computational tasks. The proposed framework demonstrates promising results through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, suggesting a significant advancement in the capabilities of QML.

title: 基于可扩展拓扑光子网络的量子密钥分发协议
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol designed specifically for scalable photonic networks. The protocol leverages the inherent advantages of a multi-hop, all-topological architecture to overcome the limitations of traditional QKD systems regarding key transmission distance and rate. We propose a scheme utilizing quantum entanglement and state transformations within the network to facilitate distributed key generation and secure key distribution. The core innovation lies in the network topology itself, which allows for robust error correction and eavesdropping detection, ultimately leading to a highly secure and high-throughput quantum communication system. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the protocol's resilience to various attack scenarios and highlights its potential for practical implementation in large-scale quantum networks.

title: The Geometry of Causality: Hierarchical Causality Networks and Predictive Geometry
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of geometry and causality, proposing a novel hierarchical causality network framework. We investigate how the structure of a network – defined by its connectivity and topology – directly influences the flow of causal influence, offering a new perspective on understanding and modeling causal relationships. The core claim is that causality is fundamentally geometric, and that the representation of a causal network via a geometric structure allows for predictive capabilities. This work utilizes a hierarchical network model to demonstrate the potential for this geometric approach to yield enhanced predictive accuracy. The analysis will delve into the mathematical foundations of this framework, focusing on network topology and flow dynamics. We will explore how the geometry inherent in the network structure enables a deeper understanding of causality than traditional, purely statistical approaches.

title: A Hybrid Approach: Combining Differentiable Simulation Engines with Reinforcement Learning Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to control and optimization of complex physical systems by integrating differentiable simulation engines with reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional control methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and nonlinearity of many physical systems, requiring extensive tuning and potentially failing to generalize well. Our methodology leverages the ability to represent physical systems as a set of differential equations, allowing for continuous, differentiable simulation. This simulation environment then serves as the basis for training an RL agent, which learns an optimal control policy through trial and error. The key innovation lies in the seamless coupling of these two techniques – the deterministic, accurate simulation providing the feedback signal for the RL agent, and the RL agent dynamically adjusting the simulation parameters to improve learning efficiency and robustness. We detail the architecture of this hybrid system, focusing on the mathematical formulation and implementation considerations. This approach offers the potential for achieving real-time control and optimization of systems that are intractable for conventional control methods. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation via Algebraic Vector Representation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge to computational efficiency. Traditional methods often struggle to efficiently handle the intricate calculations involved in quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing algebraic vector representation to transform entanglement calculations into a set of algebraic operations, aiming to dramatically improve computational speed and provide deeper insights into the fundamental nature of quantum entanglement. We establish a new method for representing entangled states as algebraic vectors, leveraging the geometric properties of string theory to achieve this transformation. The core mechanism involves the development of a specialized algebraic vector representation that allows for efficient computation through a sequence of transformations, ultimately revealing the underlying mathematical structure of entangled states. This research explores the potential for quantum entanglement computation to be revolutionized by this algorithmic shift.

title: Quantum Bayesian Network for Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Quantum Bayesian Network (QBN) architecture specifically designed for Constraint Satisfaction problems (CSPs). We propose a QBN leveraging quantum annealing or variational quantum algorithms to efficiently explore solution spaces, enabling the handling of highly complex, multi-variable CSPs. The core mechanism involves dynamically updating constraint relationships through quantum superposition, offering a potential paradigm shift in solving these challenging problems. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through a case study focusing on a simplified CSP, highlighting its ability to outperform traditional methods in terms of solution finding time and complexity. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and potential future directions of this research.

title: Distributed Differential Privacy via Federated Learning with Byzantine Resilience
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing, thereby preserving data privacy. However, existing FL frameworks are susceptible to Byzantine attacks, where malicious participants intentionally send false information to disrupt the learning process and compromise the privacy guarantees provided by differential privacy (DP). This paper proposes a novel distributed differential privacy protocol for FL that incorporates Byzantine resilience. Our approach leverages verifiable distributed computation to detect and mitigate the influence of Byzantine participants, ensuring both privacy and robustness against malicious behavior. The core claim of this work is that FL with DP is inherently vulnerable to Byzantine attacks. The primary mechanism involves designing a federated learning protocol that actively identifies and downweights contributions from potentially malicious participants. We achieve this through a combination of outlier detection techniques and verifiable computation, guaranteeing a robust and differentially private learning outcome. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of our protocol in maintaining differential privacy while mitigating the impact of Byzantine adversaries. We provide a detailed mathematical formulation of the protocol and its privacy guarantees, focusing on the key parameters and their impact on the overall privacy budget. Finally, we outline the potential implications and future research directions for this work.

title: Consistency Is Not Correctness: What Internal Contradiction Detection Certifies, Why the Entailment Is Disjunctive, and Which Decisions It Leaves Unlicensed
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Contradiction detection occupies an unusual position among proposals for making a language model check itself. Comparing two of a model's own outputs appears to need no external oracle, which makes it look like the one exception to the observation that working hallucination detectors sit outside the model. This paper argues that the appearance is produced by running two different inferences under one word. Inconsistency supports a deductive inference: if two outputs contradict each other, at least one of them is false, and this follows from logic alone without any appeal to the world. Consistency supports only an inductive one: agreement is evidence of correctness to the extent that the model's errors are unstable under whatever perturbation produced the second output, an assumption that the sampling-based detectors state explicitly and that the strongest published instance of the family declines to extend to systematic error. The two inferences have opposite properties. The deductive one is sound and disjunctive, identifying that something is wrong without identifying which output is wrong, and so licenses withholding but not repair. The inductive one names a specific output to accept, and fails in the cases that matter most, because an error shared by both compared outputs survives the comparison intact. The paper traces the consequences: that breaking the disjunction requires an adjudicator whose errors are not those of the generator, that every published route to one is external in the relevant sense even when it runs on the same weights, and that a consistency rate is a measurement of distributional stability under a named perturbation rather than a reliability figure. Making consistency an optimization target inverts its diagnostic value, which two recent results on label-free training report directly. What is not known is stated flatly, and six measurements are specified.

title: Early Detection of Digital Transaction Fraud in Banking Systems Using the Random Forest Algorithm
abstract: This research aims to develop methods for preventing and detecting cyberattacks in banking systems by leveraging machine learning techniques.[1] Cybersecurity threats are becoming increasingly complex and pose significant risks to banking institutions and their customers through various attack types including fraud, intrusion, and malware.[2][3], [4]The data science approach utilizing machine learning enables automatic and real-time identification of anomalous patterns in transactional and security log data.[2], [5] This study utilizes transaction datasets and security logs as primary data sources. Random Forest and XGBoost models were selected due to their capability to handle high-dimensional data and class imbalance. Model evaluation was conducted using accuracy, F1-score, and ROC-AUC metrics. The prototype implementation includes a visualization dashboard to assist end-users.[6], [7] Random Forest and XGBoost models are selected due to their capability to handle high-dimensional data and class imbalance.[8], [9] Systematic preprocessing and feature engineering steps will address missing values, normalization, and categorical encoding.[10], [11] Moreover, model evaluation will be conducted using metrics such as accuracy, F1-score, and ROC-AUC to ensure optimal performance.[12] The prototype system implementation includes a visualization dashboard and automatic prediction features for end-users.[13] The expected outcomes of this research are improved early detection and prevention of cyber threats in the banking sector, contributing to the advancement of AI-based security systems in Indonesia.[14] Experimental results demonstrate that tree-based ensemble learning models significantly outperform SVM in handling extreme class imbalance. XGBoost achieved the best performance with an ROC-AUC score of 0.995, followed by Random Forest at 0.992, whereas SVM achieved only 0.935. Model transparency analysis using SHAP confirmed that transaction frequency and spikes in transaction amounts were the most critical predictors for identifying fraud. Overall, this research concludes that integrating XGBoost with the SHAP approach yields a fraud detection system that offers not only high accuracy but also clear interpretability to support decision-making in the digital banking sector.

title: Quantum Algorithms for Optimization Problems in Logistics
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a quantum approach to solve hard optimization problems of logistics, such as vehicle routing, warehouse scheduling, supply chain planning, etc. Employing quantum computation models, viz., Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) as well as hybrid quantum-classical computing framework, the proposed technique overcomes problems of scalability, constraint handling, and performance issues of previous work. The research demonstrates benchmarking on benchmarks, on logistics datasets, and across quantum platforms. We establish that the solution quality and the convergence efficiency were improved by considering the quantum annealing effect, showing that quantum computing is a revolutionary playing card in optimization for logistics.

title: Digital Image Processing
abstract: Integrate machine learning and AI-based approaches into practical image processing with Python Engineers and researchers implementing image processing systems need methods that bridge classical techniques with modern machine learning approaches. This book delivers both traditional and modern AI-based methods and algorithms in image enhancement, restoration, segmentation, compression, and analysis. Written by an educator and researcher with more than 40 years’ experience in signal/image processing and machine learning, this reference provides theoretical and practical tools using the Python platform for a wide range of applications. The book consists of twenty chapters covering fundamental and advanced topics including two-dimensional image modeling, wavelet transform, Kalman filters, image reconstruction and computerized tomography, layered machines, linear and nonlinear autoencoders, and associative memories. Each chapter includes practical examples demonstrating real-world applications, supported by Python code, solution manuals, and presentation materials. This book also covers: Fundamental supervised and unsupervised machine learning methods with specific deep learning applications for image enhancement, segmentation, feature extraction, data compression, and classification Wavelet transform and filter banks integrated with state-of-the-art image analysis and processing Advanced filtering techniques including Wiener and Kalman filters, and two-dimensional image modeling Python implementations via Google colab platform enabling immediate application of theoretical concepts to practical image processing problems Instructor resources including solution manuals and presentation materials supporting adoption in digital image processing and computer vision courses Essential for professionals in industry and research laboratories requiring implementation-ready image processing methods, this reference also serves graduate students and advanced undergraduates in electrical and computer engineering, biomedical engineering, and computer science programs studying digital image processing and computer vision.

title: Structure-Token Evidence-Anchored Reasoning for Scientific Chart Understanding
abstract: Scientific charts encode quantities in axes, legends, and geometric marks, yet large vision-language models still treat them as natural photographs. Visual in-context examples do not expose the coordinate frame; unconstrained chain-of-thought can name a plausible number that was never read from a bar. We present STEER (Structure-Token Evidence-anchored Reasoning), which freezes a Llama-3.2-Vision encoder and inserts three modules: a chart structure graph encoder (CSGE) that binds ticks, legend items, and marks; evidence-anchored step reasoning (EASR) that forces every arithmetic step to cite a graph node; and weak-parser strong-reasoner alignment (WPSR) that uses a specialized table extractor only as a teacher of node attributes. On ChartQA, STEER reaches 82.70 average relaxed accuracy versus 80.16 for ChartGemma and 76.40 for a LLaVA-CoT backbone trained on the same mix. Gains widen on CharXiv reasoning (33.60 vs. 29.20 InternVL Chat V1.5) and ChartQAPro CoT (40.70 vs. 37.17 Qwen2-VL-7B), where OCR shortcuts disappear. Ablations show that dropping node serialization or numeric candidate constraints undoes most of the reasoning lift.

title: Conditional Timed Partial Orders: An Expressive and Interpretable Framework for Robot Task Specification and Planning
abstract: Timed Partial Orders (TPOs), originally proposed for workflows, provide an interpretable framework for robot task specification with planning algorithms based on mixed-integer linear programming (MILP). However, TPOs are limited in expressivity, capturing only partial-order events with simple timing constraints. In this paper, we introduce Conditional TPOs (cTPOs), which extend TPOs with richer relative-timing constraints and conditional event activations based on environmental conditions. We show that planning for cTPOs also reduces to an MILP problem; however, the added expressivity results in significantly larger MILPs that can become computationally intractable. To address this challenge, we propose a decomposition algorithm that partitions a cTPO into smaller sub-TPOs, yielding a sequence of smaller MILP problems. We prove that this decomposition is complete and preserves plan optimality while improving the interpretability of complex tasks. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of cTPOs as a task specification framework and the efficiency of our decomposition approach, achieving up to four orders of magnitude speedup over the monolithic MILP.

title: Flow3D-OPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for 3D Geometry Generation with Flow-Matching Diffusion Transformer
abstract: Recent image-to-3D generation models built on flow-matching diffusion Transformers (DiT) can produce high-fidelity meshes, yet their post-training strategy remains largely unexplored. There exist several critical bottlenecks in reinforcement learning: the inherent difficulty of defining comprehensive rewards for 3D geometric quality, and the gradient interference that arises when jointly optimizing heterogeneous objectives. Inspired by the practicability of on-policy distillation (OPD) in large language models and image generation, we propose \textbf{Flow3D-OPD}, a two-stage post-training framework that introduces multi-teacher distillation into 3D geometry generation. In the first stage, we utilize the semi-policy to enhance the foundational capability of the pretrained model and then design an agentic verifier for 3D geometric quality evaluation. Based on the verifier, we could cultivate domain-specialized teacher models via direct preference optimization (DPO). In the second stage, we consolidate heterogeneous expertise into a unified student model through on-policy distillation with hard task-routing sampling and gradient accumulation, which could mitigate the gradient interference in joint optimization. Without relying on elaborate modifications, our straightforward yet effective design achieves consistent improvements across all geometric quality dimensions and surpasses all teacher models in the average metric. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach provides an effective paradigm for reinforcement learning in 3D generation.

title: Deep Learning for Biopsy-Free Subtyping of Basal Cell Carcinoma from Dermatoscopic Images
abstract: Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) is the most common type of skin cancer, accounting for nearly 80% of skin cancer di- agnoses. Its optimal clinical management is guided by the distinct histopathologic subtype, with aggressive variants requiring more drastic measures. In current clinical practice, subtyping relies on skin biopsies, a procedure both costly and invasive. In this paper, we conduct a preliminary investigation into using deep learning for BCC subtyping, solely from a single dermatoscopic image of the lesion. Given the limited data at our disposal, we employ pre-trained vision transformers (ViTs), a state-of-the-art family of models highly effective for challenging downstream tasks with limited labeled data. Through repeated stratified k-fold cross-validation, we demonstrate that ViTs can achieve superior performance (AUC 0.784 on a dataset of 1271 dermatoscopic images of various BCC subtypes) over standard CNN-based baselines as well as previously-reported human reader perfor- mance, on the task of differentiating aggressive BCCs from other subtype families. These initial findings highlight the potential of combining deep learning and dermatoscopy to provide a biopsy- free alternative for BCC subtyping, thus aiding in improving treatment planning and patient outcomes.

title: Supplementary Code and Census Artifacts for "Quadratic relations of differentially 4-uniform permutations: a sharp displacement bound and an orbit-equivariant census"
abstract: This repository contains the computational artifacts, replication code, and census datasets accompanying the research paper: "Quadratic relations of differentially 4-uniform permutations: a sharp displacement bound and an orbit-equivariant census" by Ilhom Abdurazzokov. Abstract:The AES S-box is the multiplicative inverse on GF(2^8) composed with an affine map, and it pays for its optimal (NL, DU) = (112, 4) with algebraic structure: exactly 39 linearly independent quadratic relations. This work investigates what it costs to give some of that structure up and characterizes the exact bounds. Writing Q(F) for the quadratic relation count and d_H for the Hamming distance from the inverse map, we prove that Q is 1-Lipschitz in d_H and characterize when the bound is attained. The archive includes:- Complete enumeration and verification scripts for the d_H <= 4 neighborhood (including the 1,573,133,760 permutations at d_H = 4).- Orbit-equivariant census data for permutations commuting with multiplicative subgroup C (|C| = 85 and |C| = 51 families).- Evaluation pipelines for quadratic relation counts (Q), differential uniformity (DU), nonlinearity (NL), and boomerang uniformity (beta).

title: Dynamic Neural Networks: Adaptive Neuron Connectivity
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic neural network architecture that employs adaptive neuron connections to dynamically adjust the strength of connections based on the input data's dynamic changes. Traditional neural network models often rely on static connections, limiting their adaptability and potential for improved performance. Our proposed mechanism leverages iterative learning to automatically tune the connection weights, resulting in a more efficient and robust neural network. This work addresses the limitations of static models by enabling the network to respond intelligently to evolving data patterns. The resulting network demonstrates improved generalization capabilities and enhanced performance across a range of benchmark datasets.

title: 基于自组织网络的非线性几何模型优化器
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on a self-organizing network to refine geometric models. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, non-linear models, and the inherent noise in the optimization process can lead to suboptimal solutions. This work leverages the self-organizing network's ability to iteratively refine parameters through a process of exploration and exploitation, resulting in improved model precision and generalization capabilities. The algorithm employs a modified reinforcement learning approach, incorporating a reward function that prioritizes model accuracy while considering the network's structure, fostering a dynamic and adaptable optimization process. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, showcasing significant improvements in model convergence and accuracy compared to traditional methods.

title: Dynamic Neuron Topology Mapping and Adaptive Neuron Connection Generation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for dynamically mapping neuron topologies and generating adaptive neuron connections within neural networks. The core idea is to integrate topological network modeling with reinforcement learning to create a system capable of learning and adapting to complex neural network topologies. The system employs a multi-level modeling approach. The first level utilizes topological networks such as small-world networks and scale-free networks to represent the neural network. The second level leverages reinforcement learning algorithms, such as policy gradient or Actor-Critic, to train the connection strength between neurons. Crucially, connection strength is determined not only by neuron input/output activity but also by local topological information, including connection density and distance. A third level, an adaptive topology generation module, dynamically alters the topology structure based on network performance and learning objectives, adding or removing neurons and modifying their connections. This approach aims to optimize information processing and learning efficiency by mitigating information bottlenecks and accelerating signal propagation. The system demonstrates the potential to overcome limitations of existing neural network modeling methods and address complex learning and information processing challenges in neural networks.
